lines.translit: Strymona Maiandron te kai Istron kallireethron

i18n.en: Strymon, and Maiandros, and fair-flowing Istros,

lines.text: Φᾶσίν τε Ῥῆσόν τʼ Ἀχελώιόν τʼ ἀργυροδίνην
lines.translit: Phasin te Rhēson t' Achelōion t' argyrodinēn

i18n.en: Phasis, and Rhesos, and silver-eddying Acheloios,

lines.text: Νέσσον τε Ῥοδίον θʼ Ἁλιάκμονά θʼ Ἑπτάπορόν τε
lines.translit: Nesson te Rhodion th' Haliakmona th' Heptaporon te

i18n.en: Nessos, and Rhodios, and Haliakmon, and Heptaporos,

lines.text: Γρήνικόν τε καὶ Αἴσηπον θεῖόν τε Σιμοῦντα
lines.translit: Grēnikon te kai Aisēpon theion te Simounta

i18n.en: Granikos, and Aisepos, and divine Simoeis,

notes.official: Source-orthography note: the edition reads *Γρήνικόν* (with eta) at 342; the translation gives the standard river-name 'Granikos' (*Γράνικος*), normalizing the vowel as the name convention normalizes other variant spellings. The transliteration field follows the source (*Grēnikon*).

lines.text: Πηνειόν τε καὶ Ἕρμον ἐυρρείτην τε Κάικον
lines.translit: Pēneion te kai Hermon eurreitēn te Kaikon

i18n.en: Peneios, and Hermos, and fair-flowing Kaikos,

lines.text: Σαγγάριόν τε μέγαν Λάδωνά τε Παρθένιόν τε
lines.translit: Sangarion te megan Ladōna te Parthenion te

i18n.en: and great Sangarios, and Ladon, and Parthenios,

lines.text: Εὔηνόν τε καὶ Ἄρδησκον θεῖόν τε Σκάμανδρον.
lines.translit: Euēnon te kai Ardēskon theion te Skamandron

i18n.en: and Euenos, and Ardeskos, and divine Skamandros.

lines.text: τίκτε δὲ θυγατέρων ἱερὸν γένος, αἳ κατὰ γαῖαν
lines.translit: tikte de thygaterōn hieron genos hai kata gaian

i18n.en: And she bore a holy race of daughters, who over the earth,

lines.text: ἄνδρας κουρίζουσι σὺν Ἀπόλλωνι ἄνακτι
lines.translit: andras kourizousi syn Apollōni anakti

i18n.en: rear men to manhood, together with lord Apollo

notes.official: The river-daughters (346–348) *ἄνδρας κουρίζουσι* 'rear men to manhood' together with Apollo and the Rivers — the nurturing-of-youth motif (*kour-*) that recurs as Hekate's *kourotrophos* title at 450. Rendered 'rear men to manhood' with Evelyn-White.

lines.text: καὶ Ποταμοῖς, ταύτην δὲ Διὸς πάρα μοῖραν ἔχουσι,
lines.translit: kai Potamois tautēn de Dios para moiran echousi

i18n.en: and the Rivers; and this portion they hold from Zeus—

lines.text: Πειθώ τʼ Ἀδμήτη τε Ἰάνθη τʼ Ἠλέκτρη τε
lines.translit: Peithō t' Admētē te Ianthē t' Ēlektrē te

i18n.en: Peitho, and Admete, and Ianthe, and Elektra,

notes.official: The Okeanid catalogue (349–361) — forty-one named daughters of Okeanos and Tethys — is handled as the Nereid catalogue was (240): transparent speaking-names (*Peithō* 'Persuasion', *Ploutō* 'Wealth', *Kalliroē* 'Fair-flowing', *Ourania* 'Heavenly') are transliterated as proper names, not translated. The catalogue's inclusion of soon-to-be-major figures — *Styx* (361), *Elektra* (349), *Metis* and *Eurynome* (358), *Kalypso* (359), *Dione* (353) — is left to speak for itself.

lines.text: Δωρίς τε Πρυμνώ τε καὶ Οὐρανίη θεοειδὴς
lines.translit: Dōris te Prymnō te kai Ouraniē theoeidēs

i18n.en: and Doris, and Prymno, and godlike Ourania,

lines.text: Ἱππώ τε Κλυμένη τε Ῥόδειά τε Καλλιρόη τε
lines.translit: Hippō te Klymenē te Rhodeia te Kalliroē te

i18n.en: Hippo, and Klymene, and Rhodeia, and Kalliroe,

lines.text: Ζευξώ τε Κλυτίη τε Ἰδυῖά τε Πασιθόη τε
lines.translit: Zeuxō te Klytiē te Idyia te Pasithoē te

i18n.en: Zeuxo, and Klytie, and Idyia, and Pasithoe,

lines.text: Πληξαύρη τε Γαλαξαύρη τʼ ἐρατή τε Διώνη
lines.translit: Plēxaurē te Galaxaurē t' eratē te Diōnē

i18n.en: Plexaure, and Galaxaure, and lovely Dione,

lines.text: Μηλόβοσίς τε Φόη τε καὶ εὐειδὴς Πολυδώρη
lines.translit: Mēlobosis te Phoē te kai eueidēs Polydōrē

i18n.en: Melobosis, and Phoe, and shapely Polydora,

lines.text: Κερκηίς τε φυὴν ἐρατὴ Πλουτώ τε βοῶπις
lines.translit: Kerkēis te phyēn eratē Ploutō te boōpis

i18n.en: and Kerkeis, lovely of form, and ox-eyed Pluto,

lines.text: Περσηίς τʼ Ἰάνειρά τʼ Ἀκάστη τε Ξάνθη τε
lines.translit: Persēis t' Ianeira t' Akastē te Xanthē te

i18n.en: Perseis, and Ianeira, and Akaste, and Xanthe,

lines.text: Πετραίη τʼ ἐρόεσσα Μενεσθώ τʼ Εὐρώπη τε
lines.translit: Petraiē t' eroessa Menesthō t' Eurōpē te

i18n.en: and lovely Petraie, and Menestho, and Europe,

lines.text: Μῆτίς τʼ Εὐρυνόμη τε Τελεστώ τε Κροκοπεπλος
lines.translit: Mētis t' Eurynomē te Telestō te Krokopeplos

i18n.en: and Metis, and Eurynome, and Telesto the saffron-robed,

notes.official: *Κροκοπεπλος* (so the source, unaccented) is capitalized in the Perseus source at 358, leaving open whether it is a forty-second Okeanid name. With Evelyn-White it is read instead as the epithet *krokopeplos* 'saffron-robed' of *Telestō* — the same transparent epithet used of *Enyō* at 273 — not a separate name; the catalogue thus lists forty-one Okeanids, not forty-two. The source capitalization (and the missing accent) is not decisive, the edition capitalizing other epithets inconsistently.

lines.text: Χρυσηίς τʼ Ἀσίη τε καὶ ἱμερόεσσα Καλυψὼ
lines.translit: Chrysēis t' Asiē te kai himeroessa Kalypsō

i18n.en: Chryseis, and Asia, and lovely Kalypso,

lines.text: Εὐδώρη τε Τύχη τε καὶ Ἀμφιρὼ Ὠκυρόη τε
lines.translit: Eudōrē te Tychē te kai Amphirō Ōkyroē te

i18n.en: and Eudora, and Tyche, and Amphiro, and Okyroe,

lines.text: καὶ Στύξ, ἣ δή σφεων προφερεστάτη ἐστὶν ἁπασέων.
lines.translit: kai Styx hē dē spheōn propherestatē estin hapaseōn

i18n.en: and Styx, who is the most eminent of them all.

notes.official: *Styx* is named last of the eldest Okeanids and 'the most eminent of them all' (361, *προφερεστάτη*) — an anticipatory flag of her singular role in the poem: at 383–403 she is the first to Olympos in the Titanomachy and is made 'the great oath of the gods'. She is kept as the theonym 'Styx' per the name convention.

lines.text: αὗται δʼ Ὠκεανοῦ καὶ Τηθύος ἐξεγένοντο
lines.translit: hautai d' Ōkeanou kai Tēthyos exegenonto

i18n.en: These were born the eldest daughters of Okeanos and Tethys;

lines.text: πρεσβύταται κοῦραι· πολλαί γε μέν εἰσι καὶ ἄλλαι.
lines.translit: presbytatai kourai pollai ge men eisi kai allai

i18n.en: yet there are many others besides.

lines.text: τρὶς γὰρ χίλιαί εἰσι τανύσφυροι Ὠκεανῖναι,
lines.translit: tris gar chiliai eisi tanysphyroi Ōkeaninai

i18n.en: For there are three thousand slender-ankled Okeanids,

lines.text: αἵ ῥα πολυσπερέες γαῖαν καὶ βένθεα λίμνης
lines.translit: hai rha polysperees gaian kai benthea limnēs

i18n.en: who, widely scattered, haunt the earth and the depths of the waters

lines.text: πάντη ὁμῶς ἐφέπουσι, θεάων ἀγλαὰ τέκνα.
lines.translit: pantē homōs ephepousi theaōn aglaa tekna

i18n.en: everywhere alike, shining children of goddesses.

lines.text: τόσσοι δʼ αὖθʼ ἕτεροι ποταμοὶ καναχηδὰ ῥέοντες,
lines.translit: tossoi d' auth' heteroi potamoi kanachēda rheontes

i18n.en: And there are as many other Rivers, flowing with a ringing sound,

lines.text: υἱέες Ὠκεανοῦ, τοὺς γείνατο πότνια Τηθύς·
lines.translit: hyiees Ōkeanou tous geinato potnia Tēthys

i18n.en: sons of Okeanos, whom queenly Tethys bore;

lines.text: τῶν ὄνομʼ ἀργαλέον πάντων βροτὸν ἀνέρʼ ἐνισπεῖν,
lines.translit: tōn onom' argaleon pantōn broton aner' enispein

i18n.en: hard it is for a mortal man to tell the names of them all,

lines.text: οἳ δὲ ἕκαστοι ἴσασιν, ὅσοι περιναιετάωσιν.
lines.translit: hoi de hekastoi isasin hosoi perinaietaōsin

i18n.en: but each of those who dwell about them knows them.

lines.text: θεία δʼ Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν λαμπράν τε Σελήνην
lines.translit: theia d' Ēelion te megan lampran te Selēnēn

i18n.en: And Theia bore great Helios, and bright Selene,

notes.official: Theia bears the luminary deities *Hēlios* (Sun), *Selēnē* (Moon), and *Ēōs* (Dawn) to Hyperion (371–374). Per the name convention the three are kept as theonyms ('Helios', 'Selene', 'Eos'), not translated as the common nouns 'sun/moon/dawn', since here they are the shining powers themselves, born and acting; the Greek forms are used, not the Latin Sol/Luna/Aurora.

lines.text: Ἠῶ θʼ, ἣ πάντεσσιν ἐπιχθονίοισι φαείνει
lines.translit: Ēō th' hē pantessin epichthonioisi phaeinei

i18n.en: and Eos, who shines for all upon the earth,

lines.text: ἀθανάτοις τε θεοῖσι, τοὶ οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἔχουσι,
lines.translit: athanatois te theoisi toi ouranon euryn echousi

i18n.en: and for the immortal gods who hold the wide heaven,

lines.text: γείναθʼ ὑποδμηθεῖσʼ Ὑπερίονος ἐν φιλότητι.
lines.translit: geinath' hypodmētheis' Hyperionos en philotēti

i18n.en: having been subdued in love to Hyperion.

lines.text: Κρίῳ δʼ Εὐρυβίν τέκεν ἐν φιλότητι μιγεῖσα
lines.translit: Kriō d' Eurybin teken en philotēti migeisa

i18n.en: And Eurybia, mingling in love, bore to Krios

lines.text: Ἀστραῖόν τε μέγαν Πάλλαντά τε δῖα θεάων
lines.translit: Astraion te megan Pallanta te dia theaōn

i18n.en: great Astraios, and Pallas—she, divine among goddesses—

lines.text: Πέρσην θʼ, ὃς καὶ πᾶσι μετέπρεπεν ἰδμοσύνῃσιν.
lines.translit: Persēn th' hos kai pasi meteprepen idmosynēsin

i18n.en: and Perses, who excelled all in wisdom.

lines.text: Ἀστραίῳ δʼ Ἠὼς ἀνέμους τέκε καρτεροθύμους,
lines.translit: Astraiō d' Ēōs anemous teke karterothymous

i18n.en: And to Astraios Eos bore the strong-hearted winds,

lines.text: ἀργέστην Ζέφυρον Βορέην τʼ αἰψηροκέλευθον
lines.translit: argestēn Zephyron Boreēn t' aipsērokeleuthon

i18n.en: clearing Zephyros, and swift-coursing Boreas,

lines.text: καὶ Νότον, ἐν φιλότητι θεὰ θεῷ εὐνηθεῖσα.
lines.translit: kai Noton en philotēti thea theō eunētheisa

i18n.en: and Notos—a goddess bedded in love with a god.

lines.text: τοὺς δὲ μέτʼ ἀστέρα τίκτεν Ἑωσφόρον Ἠριγένεια
lines.translit: tous de met' astera tikten Heōsphoron Ērigeneia

i18n.en: And after them Erigeneia bore the star Eosphoros,

lines.text: ἄστρα τε λαμπετόωντα, τά τʼ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται.
lines.translit: astra te lampetoōnta ta t' ouranos estephanōtai

i18n.en: and the shining stars with which heaven is crowned.

lines.text: Στὺξ δʼ ἔτεκʼ Ὠκεανοῦ θυγάτηρ Πάλλαντι μιγεῖσα
lines.translit: Styx d' etek' Ōkeanou thygatēr Pallanti migeisa

i18n.en: And Styx, daughter of Okeanos, mingling with Pallas,

lines.text: Ζῆλον καὶ Νίκην καλλίσφυρον ἐν μεγάροισιν·
lines.translit: Zēlon kai Nikēn kallisphyron en megaroisin

i18n.en: bore Zelos and fair-ankled Nike in her halls;

lines.text: καὶ Κράτος ἠδὲ Βίην ἀριδείκετα γείνατο τέκνα,
lines.translit: kai Kratos ēde Biēn arideiketa geinato tekna

i18n.en: and she bore Kratos and Bia, renowned children,

lines.text: τῶν οὐκ ἔστʼ ἀπάνευθε Διὸς δόμος, οὐδέ τις ἕδρη,
lines.translit: tōn ouk est' apaneuthe Dios domos oude tis hedrē

i18n.en: who have no house apart from Zeus, nor any seat,

lines.text: οὐδʼ ὁδός, ὅππη μὴ κείνοις θεὸς ἡγεμονεύῃ,
lines.translit: oud' hodos hoppē mē keinois theos hēgemoneuē

i18n.en: nor any way, save where the god leads them,

lines.text: ἀλλʼ αἰεὶ πὰρ Ζηνὶ βαρυκτύπῳ ἑδριόωνται.
lines.translit: all' aiei par Zēni baryktypō hedrioōntai

i18n.en: but ever they sit beside deep-thundering Zeus.

lines.text: ὣς γὰρ ἐβούλευσεν Στὺξ ἄφθιτος Ὠκεανίνη
lines.translit: hōs gar ebouleusen Styx aphthitos Ōkeaninē

i18n.en: For thus did imperishable Styx, the Okeanid, purpose

lines.text: ἤματι τῷ, ὅτε πάντας Ὀλύμπιος ἀστεροπητὴς
lines.translit: ēmati tō hote pantas Olympios asteropētēs

i18n.en: on that day when the Olympian, the lightning-hurler,

lines.text: ἀθανάτους ἐκάλεσσε θεοὺς ἐς μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον,
lines.translit: athanatous ekalesse theous es makron Olympon

i18n.en: called all the immortal gods to high Olympos,

lines.text: εἶπε δʼ, ὃς ἂν μετὰ εἷο θεῶν Τιτῆσι μάχοιτο,
lines.translit: eipe d' hos an meta heio theōn Titēsi machoito

i18n.en: and said that whoever of the gods would fight with him against the Titans,

lines.text: μή τινʼ ἀπορραίσειν γεράων, τιμὴν δὲ ἕκαστον
lines.translit: mē tin' aporraisein geraōn timēn de hekaston

i18n.en: he would not strip of his prerogatives, but each

notes.official: Zeus's accession-offer (392–396) introduces the poem's *apportioned-honour* lexicon, which then saturates the Hekate hymn: *timē* 'honour/privilege', *geras* (pl. *gerea*) 'prerogative', with their privatives *atimos* 'without honour' and *agerastos* 'without prerogative' (395). The translation fixes a consistent English mapping across the block — *timē* 'honour', *geras* 'prerogative', *moira* 'share' (413), *aisa* 'allotted part' (422), *dasmos* 'division' (425), *olbos* 'wealth' (420) — so that the hymn's argument (that Hekate's share under Zeus is undiminished) reads as a single thematic thread; this follows Evelyn-White's renderings while regularizing them.

lines.text: ἑξέμεν, ἣν τὸ πάρος γε μετʼ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν
lines.translit: hexemen hēn to paros ge met' athanatoisi theoisin

i18n.en: should keep the honor he had before among the immortal gods;

lines.text: τὸν δʼ ἔφαθʼ, ὅστις ἄτιμος ὑπὸ Κρόνου ἠδʼ ἀγέραστος,
lines.translit: ton d' ephath' hostis atimos hypo Kronou ēd' agerastos

i18n.en: and whoever was without honor and without prerogative under Kronos,

lines.text: τιμῆς καὶ γεράων ἐπιβησέμεν, ἧ θέμις ἐστίν.
lines.translit: timēs kai geraōn epibēsemen hē themis estin

i18n.en: him he would set upon honor and prerogatives, as is right.

lines.text: ἦλθε δʼ ἄρα πρώτη Στὺξ ἄφθιτος Οὔλυμπόνδε
lines.translit: ēlthe d' ara prōtē Styx aphthitos Oulymponde

i18n.en: So imperishable Styx came first to Olympos,

lines.text: σὺν σφοῖσιν παίδεσσι φίλου διὰ μήδεα πατρός.
lines.translit: syn sphoisin paidessi philou dia mēdea patros

i18n.en: with her own children, through the counsels of her dear father.

lines.text: τὴν δὲ Ζεὺς τίμησε, περισσὰ δὲ δῶρα δέδωκεν.
lines.translit: tēn de Zeus timēse perissa de dōra dedōken

i18n.en: And Zeus honored her, and gave her surpassing gifts.

lines.text: αὐτὴν μὲν γὰρ ἔθηκε θεῶν μέγαν ἔμμεναι ὅρκον,
lines.translit: autēn men gar ethēke theōn megan emmenai horkon

i18n.en: For he made her to be the great oath of the gods,

notes.official: Zeus makes Styx *theōn megan horkon*, 'the great oath of the gods' (400): the water of Styx becomes the inviolable oath-witness *by which* the gods swear (elaborated at 775–806, Block D). Here *horkos* is the oath sworn *by* — the sanction-object — not the avenging deity *Horkos* personified among Eris's children at 231–232; with Evelyn-White it is rendered 'oath' (lower case), the two senses kept distinct and *horkos* not capitalized. The rendering stays at the philological level; the passage's interest for the poem is Zeus's institution of a binding cosmic sanction, and no reading is pressed beyond that.

lines.text: παῖδας δʼ ἤματα πάντα ἑοῦ μεταναιέτας εἶναι.
lines.translit: paidas d' ēmata panta heou metanaietas einai

i18n.en: and her children to dwell with him for all their days.

lines.text: ὣς δʼ αὔτως πάντεσσι διαμπερές, ὥς περ ὑπέστη,
lines.translit: hōs d' autōs pantessi diamperes hōs per hypestē

i18n.en: And even as he promised, so he fulfilled it utterly to all;

lines.text: ἐξετέλεσσʼ· αὐτὸς δὲ μέγα κρατεῖ ἠδὲ ἀνάσσει.
lines.translit: exeteless' autos de mega kratei ēde anassei

i18n.en: but he himself holds great power and is lord.

lines.text: φοίβη δʼ αὖ Κοίου πολυήρατον ἦλθεν ἐς εὐνήν·
lines.translit: phoibē d' au Koiou polyēraton ēlthen es eunēn

i18n.en: And Phoibe, in turn, came to the much-loved bed of Koios;

lines.text: κυσαμένη δὴ ἔπειτα θεὰ θεοῦ ἐν φιλότητι
lines.translit: kysamenē dē epeita thea theou en philotēti

i18n.en: and then the goddess, conceiving in the love of the god,

lines.text: Λητὼ κυανόπεπλον ἐγείνατο, μείλιχον αἰεί,
lines.translit: Lētō kyanopeplon egeinato meilichon aiei

i18n.en: bore dark-robed Leto, ever gentle,

lines.text: ἤπιον ἀνθρώποισι καὶ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν,
lines.translit: ēpion anthrōpoisi kai athanatoisi theoisin

i18n.en: kindly to men and to the immortal gods,

lines.text: μείλιχον ἐξ ἀρχῆς, ἀγανώτατον ἐντὸς Ὀλύμπου.
lines.translit: meilichon ex archēs aganōtaton entos Olympou

i18n.en: gentle from the beginning, the mildest within Olympos.

lines.text: γείνατο δʼ Ἀστερίην ἐυώνυμον, ἥν ποτε Πέρσης
lines.translit: geinato d' Asteriēn euōnymon hēn pote Persēs

i18n.en: And she bore well-named Asteria, whom once Perses

lines.text: ἠγάγετʼ ἐς μέγα δῶμα φίλην κεκλῆσθαι ἄκοιτιν.
lines.translit: ēgaget' es mega dōma philēn keklēsthai akoitin

i18n.en: led to his great house to be called his dear wife.

lines.text: ἢ δʼ ὑποκυσαμένη Ἑκάτην τέκε, τὴν περὶ πάντων
lines.translit: ē d' hypokysamenē Hekatēn teke tēn peri pantōn

i18n.en: And she conceived and bore Hekate, whom above all

notes.official: The Hekate hymn (411–452) — the longest single-god passage in the *Theogony*, and much discussed as a possible Hesiodic set-piece on divine prerogative — praises the goddess as one honoured by Zeus across *earth, sea and starry heaven* (413–414, 427) with a share (*timē*, *geras*, *moira*) in every sphere. The framing claim is that Zeus, far from stripping the daughter of a Titan (Asteria) of her ancestral honours, confirms and enlarges them. Individual cruxes are handled at their lines: the honour-lexicon at 393/413, *mounogenēs* 'only child' at 426/448, *kourotrophos* 'nurse of the young' at 450.

lines.text: Ζεὺς Κρονίδης τίμησε· πόρεν δέ οἱ ἀγλαὰ δῶρα,
lines.translit: Zeus Kronidēs timēse poren de hoi aglaa dōra

i18n.en: Zeus, son of Kronos, honored; and he gave her splendid gifts,

lines.text: μοῖραν ἔχειν γαίης τε καὶ ἀτρυγέτοιο θαλάσσης.
lines.translit: moiran echein gaiēs te kai atrygetoio thalassēs

i18n.en: to have a share of the earth and of the barren sea.

lines.text: ἣ δὲ καὶ ἀστερόεντος ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἔμμορε τιμῆς
lines.translit: hē de kai asteroentos ap' ouranou emmore timēs

i18n.en: And she has received honor also from the starry heaven,

lines.text: ἀθανάτοις τε θεοῖσι τετιμένη ἐστὶ μάλιστα.
lines.translit: athanatois te theoisi tetimenē esti malista

i18n.en: and is honored most of all by the immortal gods.

lines.text: καὶ γὰρ νῦν, ὅτε πού τις ἐπιχθονίων ἀνθρώπων
lines.translit: kai gar nyn hote pou tis epichthoniōn anthrōpōn

i18n.en: For even now, whenever any of men upon the earth,

lines.text: ἔρδων ἱερὰ καλὰ κατὰ νόμον ἱλάσκηται,
lines.translit: erdōn hiera kala kata nomon hilaskētai

i18n.en: doing fair sacrifice according to custom, seeks grace,

lines.text: κικλῄσκει Ἑκάτην. πολλή τέ οἱ ἕσπετο τιμὴ
lines.translit: kiklēskei Hekatēn pollē te hoi hespeto timē

i18n.en: he calls upon Hekate. And great honor readily attends

lines.text: ῥεῖα μάλʼ, ᾧ πρόφρων γε θεὰ ὑποδέξεται εὐχάς,
lines.translit: rheia mal' hō prophrōn ge thea hypodexetai euchas

i18n.en: that man whose prayers the goddess graciously receives,

lines.text: καί τέ οἱ ὄλβον ὀπάζει, ἐπεὶ δύναμίς γε πάρεστιν.
lines.translit: kai te hoi olbon opazei epei dynamis ge parestin

i18n.en: and she grants him wealth, for the power is hers.

lines.text: ὅσσοι γὰρ Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἐξεγένοντο
lines.translit: hossoi gar Gaiēs te kai Ouranou exegenonto

i18n.en: For of all who were born of Gaia and Ouranos

lines.text: καὶ τιμὴν ἔλαχον, τούτων ἔχει αἶσαν ἁπάντων.
lines.translit: kai timēn elachon toutōn echei aisan hapantōn

i18n.en: and received honor, of all these she has her allotted part.

lines.text: οὐδέ τί μιν Κρονίδης ἐβιήσατο οὐδέ τʼ ἀπηύρα,
lines.translit: oude ti min Kronidēs ebiēsato oude t' apēura

i18n.en: Nor did the son of Kronos do her violence, nor take from her

lines.text: ὅσσʼ ἔλαχεν Τιτῆσι μετὰ προτέροισι θεοῖσιν,
lines.translit: hoss' elachen Titēsi meta proteroisi theoisin

i18n.en: aught of what she had as her lot among the Titans, the earlier gods,

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ἔχει, ὡς τὸ πρῶτον ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς ἔπλετο δασμός,
lines.translit: all' echei hōs to prōton ap' archēs epleto dasmos

i18n.en: but she keeps it, as the division was at the first, from the beginning,

lines.text: καὶ γέρας ἐν γαίῃ τε καὶ οὐρανῷ ἠδὲ θαλάσσῃ·
lines.translit: kai geras en gaiē te kai ouranō ēde thalassē

i18n.en: and a prerogative in earth and in heaven and in sea.

notes.official: Lines 426 and 427 are printed in the transposed order 427–426 (West 1966 / Perseus), so the *refId* sequence is deliberately non-ascending: 427 completes the 'earth, heaven and sea' tricolon of 413–414 before 426 resumes the *mounogenēs* thought. Editorial and text-critical, not a translation choice. On *geras* 'prerogative' here, see 393.

lines.text: οὐδʼ, ὅτι μουνογενής, ἧσσον θεὰ ἔμμορε τιμῆς,
lines.translit: oud' hoti mounogenēs hēsson thea emmore timēs

i18n.en: Nor, because she is an only child, has the goddess less honor,

notes.official: *μουνογενής* (426; Ionic for *monogenēs*, *mono-* 'single/only' + *gen-* 'born'), 'only child, single-born': the pivot of the whole hymn — that Hekate, an *only* child of a single mother (Asteria, with no sibling to share the ancestral honours), nonetheless holds an undiminished portion in every domain. With Evelyn-White the translation renders 'only child' (so too *μουνογενὴς ἐκ μητρός* 'only child from her mother', 448). The later Christian use of the same lexeme *monogenēs* of Christ — Vulgate *unigenitus*, English 'only-begotten' (John 1:14, 3:16) — is a datum of the word's reception history, not of Hesiod's sense here; the theologically loaded 'only-begotten' is deliberately kept out of the translated line, which says only what the Greek says. The reception link is recorded in the glossary and cross-referenced to the central *yechid-only-one-formula* entry, but neither text governs the other.

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ἔτι καὶ πολὺ μᾶλλον, ἐπεὶ Ζεὺς τίεται αὐτήν.
lines.translit: all' eti kai poly mallon epei Zeus tietai autēn

i18n.en: but far more, since Zeus holds her in honor.

lines.text: ᾧ δʼ ἐθέλει, μεγάλως παραγίγνεται ἠδʼ ὀνίνησιν·
lines.translit: hō d' ethelei megalōs paragignetai ēd' oninēsin

i18n.en: To whom she will, she comes near greatly and gives aid;

lines.text: ἔν τε δίκῃ βασιλεῦσι παρʼ αἰδοίοισι καθίζει,
lines.translit: en te dikē basileusi par' aidoioisi kathizei

i18n.en: and in judgment she sits beside reverend kings;

notes.official: Lines 430 and 434 are printed in the transposed order 434–430 (West 1966 / Perseus); the *refId* sequence is non-ascending by design. 434 ('in judgment she sits beside reverend kings') and 430 ('in the assembly … preeminent among the people') are consecutive clauses of Hekate's civic sphere, reordered by the editor.

lines.text: ἔν τʼ ἀγορῇ λαοῖσι μεταπρέπει, ὅν κʼ ἐθέλῃσιν·
lines.translit: en t' agorē laoisi metaprepei hon k' ethelēsin

i18n.en: and in the assembly, whom she will is preeminent among the people;

lines.text: ἠδʼ ὁπότʼ ἐς πόλεμον φθεισήνορα θωρήσσωνται
lines.translit: ēd' hopot' es polemon phtheisēnora thōrēssōntai

i18n.en: and when men arm for man-destroying war,

lines.text: ἀνέρες, ἔνθα θεὰ παραγίγνεται, οἷς κʼ ἐθέλῃσι
lines.translit: aneres entha thea paragignetai hois k' ethelēsi

i18n.en: there the goddess stands by those she wills,

lines.text: νίκην προφρονέως ὀπάσαι καὶ κῦδος ὀρέξαι.
lines.translit: nikēn prophroneōs opasai kai kydos orexai

i18n.en: graciously to grant them victory and to hold out glory.

lines.text: ἐσθλὴ δʼ αὖθʼ ὁπότʼ ἄνδρες ἀεθλεύωσιν ἀγῶνι,
lines.translit: esthlē d' auth' hopot' andres aethleuōsin agōni

i18n.en: Good is she too when men contend in the games:

lines.text: ἔνθα θεὰ καὶ τοῖς παραγίγνεται ἠδʼ ὀνίνησιν·
lines.translit: entha thea kai tois paragignetai ēd' oninēsin

i18n.en: there also the goddess stands by them and gives aid;

lines.text: νικήσας δὲ βίῃ καὶ κάρτεϊ καλὸν ἄεθλον
lines.translit: nikēsas de biē kai kartei kalon aethlon

i18n.en: and he who wins by force and strength, the fair prize

lines.text: ῥεῖα φέρει χαίρων τε, τοκεῦσι δὲ κῦδος ὀπάζει.
lines.translit: rheia pherei chairōn te tokeusi de kydos opazei

i18n.en: easily and joyfully bears off, and gives glory to his parents.

lines.text: ἐσθλὴ δʼ ἱππήεσσι παρεστάμεν, οἷς κʼ ἐθέλῃσιν.
lines.translit: esthlē d' hippēessi parestamen hois k' ethelēsin

i18n.en: Good is she to stand by horsemen, whom she will.

lines.text: καὶ τοῖς, οἳ γλαυκὴν δυσπέμφελον ἐργάζονται,
lines.translit: kai tois hoi glaukēn dyspemphelon ergazontai

i18n.en: And to those who work the grey, stormy sea,

lines.text: εὔχονται δʼ Ἑκάτῃ καὶ ἐρικτύπῳ Ἐννοσιγαίῳ,
lines.translit: euchontai d' Hekatē kai eriktypō Ennosigaiō

i18n.en: and who pray to Hekate and to the loud-crashing Earth-Shaker,

lines.text: ῥηιδίως ἄγρην κυδρὴ θεὸς ὤπασε πολλήν,
lines.translit: rhēidiōs agrēn kydrē theos ōpase pollēn

i18n.en: readily the glorious goddess grants a great catch,

lines.text: ῥεῖα δʼ ἀφείλετο φαινομένην, ἐθέλουσά γε θυμῷ.
lines.translit: rheia d' apheileto phainomenēn ethelousa ge thymō

i18n.en: and readily she takes it away when it appears, if so she wills in her heart.

lines.text: ἐσθλὴ δʼ ἐν σταθμοῖσι σὺν Ἑρμῇ ληίδʼ ἀέξειν·
lines.translit: esthlē d' en stathmoisi syn Hermē lēid' aexein

i18n.en: Good is she, with Hermes, to increase the stock in the steadings;

lines.text: βουκολίας δʼ ἀγέλας τε καὶ αἰπόλια πλατέʼ αἰγῶν
lines.translit: boukolias d' agelas te kai aipolia plate' aigōn

i18n.en: the herds of cattle, and the wide droves of goats,

lines.text: ποίμνας τʼ εἰροπόκων ὀίων, θυμῷ γʼ ἐθέλουσα,
lines.translit: poimnas t' eiropokōn oiōn thymō g' ethelousa

i18n.en: and the flocks of wooly sheep, if so she wills in her heart,

lines.text: ἐξ ὀλίγων βριάει κἀκ πολλῶν μείονα θῆκεν.
lines.translit: ex oligōn briaei kak pollōn meiona thēken

i18n.en: she makes great from few, and from many makes them fewer.

lines.text: οὕτω τοι καὶ μουνογενὴς ἐκ μητρὸς ἐοῦσα
lines.translit: houtō toi kai mounogenēs ek mētros eousa

i18n.en: Thus, though she is an only child from her mother,

notes.official: See on 426: *μουνογενὴς ἐκ μητρός* 'an only child from her mother' restates the hymn's thesis at its close; 'only child' is kept, 'only-begotten' declined.

lines.text: πᾶσι μετʼ ἀθανάτοισι τετίμηται γεράεσσιν.
lines.translit: pasi met' athanatoisi tetimētai geraessin

i18n.en: she is honored among all the immortals with prerogatives.

lines.text: θῆκε δέ μιν Κρονίδης κουροτρόφον, οἳ μετʼ ἐκείνην
lines.translit: thēke de min Kronidēs kourotrophon hoi met' ekeinēn

i18n.en: And the son of Kronos made her a nurse of the young, of all who after her

notes.official: Zeus makes Hekate *kourotrophos* (450, 452), 'nurse/rearer of the young' — a widespread Greek cult-title (borne also by Gaia, Hestia, Artemis) here extended to *all* who 'after her beheld the light of Eos', i.e. every mortal born thereafter. With Evelyn-White the translation renders 'nurse of the young'; the cult-title is not transliterated. The nurturing role echoes the river-daughters who *κουρίζουσι* 'rear men to manhood' at 346–348 (the same *kour-* root). The rendering stays at the lexical level and does not press the *rearer-of-the-young* motif beyond what the cult-title states.

lines.text: ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ἴδοντο φάος πολυδερκέος Ἠοῦς.
lines.translit: ophthalmoisin idonto phaos polyderkeos Ēous

i18n.en: beheld with their eyes the light of far-seeing Eos.

lines.text: οὕτως ἐξ ἀρχῆς κουροτρόφος, αἳ δέ τε τιμαί.
lines.translit: houtōs ex archēs kourotrophos hai de te timai

i18n.en: So from the beginning she is a nurse of the young; and these are her honors.

notes.official: See on 450: *kourotrophos* 'nurse of the young' closes the hymn, resuming 450; *αἳ δέ τε τιμαί* 'and these are her honours' rounds off the apportioned-honour theme (393, 413).

lines.text: Ῥείη δὲ δμηθεῖσα Κρόνῳ τέκε φαίδιμα τέκνα,
lines.translit: Rheiē de dmētheisa Kronō teke phaidima tekna

i18n.en: And Rhea, subdued by Kronos, bore splendid children:

notes.official: The Kronos–Rhea theogony opens. *Ῥείη* (Rhea) is kept in the surface form 'Rhea' established in Block A (135), the standard transliteration of the goddess's name against the source's Ionic *Ῥείη*; *δμηθεῖσα* 'subdued, mastered' is the stock formula for a goddess bearing to a consort. No divergence from Evelyn-White.

lines.text: Ἱστίην Δήμητρα καὶ Ἥρην χρυσοπέδιλον
lines.translit: Histiēn Dēmētra kai Hērēn chrysopedilon

i18n.en: Hestia, Demeter, and golden-sandalled Hera,

notes.official: Two dialectal theonyms in the Kronides roster are normalized to their standard forms, with the source spellings kept verbatim in the text field. *Ἱστίην* (454, the Ionic form) is rendered 'Hestia', and *Ἀίδην* (455, the epic form without the rough breathing) is rendered 'Hades' — both the panhellenic Greek forms, not Latinizations (which would be Vesta, Pluto/Dis). This parallels the entry-governed *Γῆ*→Gaia (106) and *Γρήνικον*→Granikos (342) normalizations of Blocks A–B; see the overlay entry `dialectal-theonym-normalization-theogony`.

lines.text: ἴφθιμόν τʼ Ἀίδην, ὃς ὑπὸ χθονὶ δώματα ναίει
lines.translit: iphthimon t' Aidēn hos hypo chthoni dōmata naiei

i18n.en: and mighty Hades, who dwells in halls beneath the earth

notes.official: See on 454: *Ἀίδην* (epic, unaspirated) → 'Hades', the standard form; *ὃς ὑπὸ χθονὶ δώματα ναίει* 'who dwells in halls beneath the earth' marks his chthonic domain.

lines.text: νηλεὲς ἦτορ ἔχων, καὶ ἐρίκτυπον Ἐννοσίγαιον
lines.translit: nēlees ētor echōn kai eriktypon Ennosigaion

i18n.en: with a pitiless heart, and the loud-crashing Earth-Shaker,

notes.official: *ἐρίκτυπον Ἐννοσίγαιον* 'the loud-crashing Earth-Shaker' designates Poseidon, who is not named here; with Evelyn-White the epithet-title is rendered literally and the proper name is not substituted, matching the treatment established at 441 (Block B). See the overlay entry `periphrastic-title-unnamed-god-theogony`; this resolves the Ennosigaios half of the THEO-571 question.

lines.text: Ζῆνά τε μητιόεντα, θεῶν πατέρʼ ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν,
lines.translit: Zēna te mētioenta theōn pater' ēde kai andrōn

i18n.en: and Zeus the counsellor, father of gods and men,

lines.text: τοῦ καὶ ὑπὸ βροντῆς πελεμίζεται εὐρεῖα χθών.
lines.translit: tou kai hypo brontēs pelemizetai eureia chthōn

i18n.en: at whose thunder the wide earth is shaken.

lines.text: καὶ τοὺς μὲν κατέπινε μέγας Κρόνος, ὥς τις ἕκαστος
lines.translit: kai tous men katepine megas Kronos hōs tis hekastos

i18n.en: And these great Kronos swallowed down, as each

lines.text: νηδύος ἐξ ἱερῆς μητρὸς πρὸς γούναθʼ ἵκοιτο,
lines.translit: nēdyos ex hierēs mētros pros gounath' hikoito

i18n.en: came from the holy womb to its mother's knees,

lines.text: τὰ φρονέων, ἵνα μή τις ἀγαυῶν Οὐρανιώνων
lines.translit: ta phroneōn hina mē tis agauōn Ouraniōnōn

i18n.en: with this intent, that none other of the proud descendants of Ouranos

lines.text: ἄλλος ἐν ἀθανάτοισιν ἔχοι βασιληίδα τιμήν.
lines.translit: allos en athanatoisin echoi basilēida timēn

i18n.en: should hold the kingly honour among the immortals.

notes.official: *βασιληΐδα τιμήν* 'the kingly honour' (462), and *τιμῆς … ἐξελάειν* 'drive him from his honour' (491), are rendered 'honour' consistently with the *timē*→'honour' mapping of the Block-B honour-vocabulary entry (`time-geras-moira-honor-vocabulary-theogony`), but that entry is deliberately NOT applied here. Its scope is the apportionment of divine prerogative among many gods (the accession-offer and the Hekate hymn, 392–452); the Block-C *βασιληΐς τιμή* is instead the singular *royal* honour — kingship itself — which belongs conceptually with the *kratos/phertatos* sovereignty vocabulary (49, 647, 662) rather than with the shared-out *gerea/timai*. The rendering stays consistent; the entry-scope boundary is recorded here (resolving THEO-462).

lines.text: πεύθετο γὰρ Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος,
lines.translit: peutheto gar Gaiēs te kai Ouranou asteroentos

i18n.en: For he had learned from Gaia and starry Ouranos

notes.official: *πεύθετο … Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος* 'he had learned from Gaia and starry Ouranos' the prophecy (463–465) that Kronos was fated to be overcome by his own son. This is the first Block-C instance of a recurring motif: Gaia as the source of the prophetic counsel that drives each divine succession — restated at 475, and reappearing as *Γαίης ἐννεσίῃσι πολυφραδέεσσι* 'the shrewd promptings of Gaia' (494) and *Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσιν* 'the counsels of Gaia' (626), anticipating her counsel again at 884 (Block D). The vocabulary is rendered literally with Evelyn-White; see the overlay entry `gaia-counsel-prophecy-vocabulary-theogony` (resolving THEO-626). **Lens-discipline note:** Gaia as the earth-power whose foreknowledge steers each regime change is a Wheel-of-Heaven-salient motif, but the rendering and the note stay at the lexical level and press no cosmological reading into the line.

lines.text: οὕνεκά οἱ πέπρωτο ἑῷ ὑπὸ παιδὶ δαμῆναι
lines.translit: houneka hoi peprōto heō hypo paidi damēnai

i18n.en: that it was fated for him to be overcome by his own son,

lines.text: καὶ κρατερῷ περ ἐόντι, Διὸς μεγάλου διὰ βουλάς·
lines.translit: kai kraterō per eonti Dios megalou dia boulas

i18n.en: strong though he was, through the plans of great Zeus.

lines.text: τῷ ὅ γʼ ἄρʼ οὐκ ἀλαὸς σκοπιὴν ἔχεν, ἀλλὰ δοκεύων
lines.translit: tō ho g' ar' ouk alaos skopiēn echen alla dokeuōn

i18n.en: Therefore he kept no blind watch, but watching

lines.text: παῖδας ἑοὺς κατέπινε· Ῥέην δʼ ἔχε πένθος ἄλαστον.
lines.translit: paidas heous katepine Rheēn d' eche penthos alaston

i18n.en: he swallowed down his own children; and unforgettable grief held Rhea.

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ὅτε δὴ Δίʼ ἔμελλε θεῶν πατέρʼ ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν
lines.translit: all' hote dē Di' emelle theōn pater' ēde kai andrōn

i18n.en: But when she was about to bear Zeus, the father of gods and men,

lines.text: τέξεσθαι, τότʼ ἔπειτα φίλους λιτάνευε τοκῆας
lines.translit: texesthai tot' epeita philous litaneue tokēas

i18n.en: then she besought her own dear parents,

lines.text: τοὺς αὐτῆς, Γαῖάν τε καὶ Οὐρανὸν ἀστερόεντα,
lines.translit: tous autēs Gaian te kai Ouranon asteroenta

i18n.en: Gaia and starry Ouranos,

lines.text: μῆτιν συμφράσσασθαι, ὅπως λελάθοιτο τεκοῦσα
lines.translit: mētin symphrassasthai hopōs lelathoito tekousa

i18n.en: to devise a plan with her, so that she might bring forth her dear child unnoticed,

lines.text: παῖδα φίλον, τίσαιτο δʼ ἐρινῦς πατρὸς ἑοῖο
lines.translit: paida philon tisaito d' erinys patros heoio

i18n.en: and that she might exact requital for the avenging spirits of her own father

lines.text: παίδων θʼ, οὓς κατέπινε μέγας Κρόνος ἀγκυλομήτης.
lines.translit: paidōn th' hous katepine megas Kronos ankylomētēs

i18n.en: and of the children whom great Kronos of the crooked counsel swallowed down.

lines.text: οἳ δὲ θυγατρὶ φίλῃ μάλα μὲν κλύον ἠδʼ ἐπίθοντο,
lines.translit: hoi de thygatri philē mala men klyon ēd' epithonto

i18n.en: And they readily heard and obeyed their dear daughter,

lines.text: καί οἱ πεφραδέτην, ὅσα περ πέπρωτο γενέσθαι
lines.translit: kai hoi pephradetēn hosa per peprōto genesthai

i18n.en: and told her all that was fated to come to pass

notes.official: See on 463: *καί οἱ πεφραδέτην, ὅσα περ πέπρωτο γενέσθαι* 'they told her all that was fated to come to pass' — the second link in the Gaia-and-Ouranos counsel/prophecy motif tracked by `gaia-counsel-prophecy-vocabulary-theogony`.

lines.text: ἀμφὶ Κρόνῳ βασιλῆι καὶ υἱέι καρτεροθύμῳ.
lines.translit: amphi Kronō basilēi kai hyiei karterothymō

i18n.en: concerning Kronos the king and his strong-hearted son.

lines.text: πέμψαν δʼ ἐς Λύκτον, Κρήτης ἐς πίονα δῆμον,
lines.translit: pempsan d' es Lykton Krētēs es piona dēmon

i18n.en: And they sent her to Lyktos, to the rich land of Krete,

notes.official: *Κρήτη* is rendered 'Krete', the Greek form, NOT the familiar English exonym 'Crete' — a surface divergence from Evelyn-White. This follows the signed-off Block-B river-catalogue precedent (Greek forms even over entrenched exonyms: Neilos-not-Nile, Istros-not-Danube), and the closer Block-A island precedent *Kypros*-not-Cyprus; 'Crete' is the Latin-derived exonym (via *Creta*), 'Krete' the transliteration of *Κρήτη*. The other Block-C toponyms are likewise given in Greek forms — *Λύκτον* 'Lyktos' (477, 482), *Αἰγαῖον* 'Mount Aigaion' (484), *Πυθώ* 'Pytho' (499), *Παρνησοῖο* 'Parnassos' (499). See the overlay entry `place-name-greek-forms-block-c-theogony` (resolving THEO-477). Flagged for the reviewer as a familiar-exonym judgement call.

lines.text: ὁππότʼ ἄρʼ ὁπλότατον παίδων τέξεσθαι ἔμελλε,
lines.translit: hoppot' ar' hoplotaton paidōn texesthai emelle

i18n.en: when she was about to bear the youngest of her children,

lines.text: Ζῆνα μέγαν· τὸν μέν οἱ ἐδέξατο Γαῖα πελώρη
lines.translit: Zēna megan ton men hoi edexato Gaia pelōrē

i18n.en: great Zeus. Him did huge Gaia receive from her

lines.text: Κρήτῃ ἐν εὐρείῃ τραφέμεν ἀτιταλλέμεναί τε.
lines.translit: Krētē en eureiē traphemen atitallemenai te

i18n.en: in wide Krete, to nurse and to rear.

notes.official: See on 477: *Κρήτῃ ἐν εὐρείῃ* 'in wide Krete', the Greek form retained.

lines.text: ἔνθα μιν ἷκτο φέρουσα θοὴν διὰ νύκτα μέλαιναν
lines.translit: entha min hikto pherousa thoēn dia nykta melainan

i18n.en: There she came, carrying him through the swift black night,

lines.text: πρώτην ἐς Λύκτον· κρύψεν δέ ἑ χερσὶ λαβοῦσα
lines.translit: prōtēn es Lykton krypsen de he chersi labousa

i18n.en: first to Lyktos; and she took him in her arms and hid him

lines.text: ἄντρῳ ἐν ἠλιβάτῳ, ζαθέης ὑπὸ κεύθεσι γαίης,
lines.translit: antrō en ēlibatō zatheēs hypo keuthesi gaiēs

i18n.en: in a steep cave, beneath the secret places of the holy earth,

lines.text: Αἰγαίῳ ἐν ὄρει πεπυκασμένῳ ὑλήεντι.
lines.translit: Aigaiō en orei pepykasmenō hylēenti

i18n.en: on Mount Aigaion, thick with woods.

notes.official: *Αἰγαῖον ὄρος* 'Mount Aigaion', the Greek form, is the wooded height of Zeus's concealment; the Cretan localization varies in the tradition (Ida, Dikte, Aigaion — West 1966), but the text names Aigaion and the surface follows it. Governed by `place-name-greek-forms-block-c-theogony`.

lines.text: τῷ δὲ σπαργανίσασα μέγαν λίθον ἐγγυάλιξεν
lines.translit: tō de sparganisasa megan lithon engyalixen

i18n.en: But to him she gave a great stone wrapped in swaddling-clothes,

notes.official: *μέγαν λίθον … σπαργανίσασα* 'a great stone wrapped in swaddling-clothes' is given to Kronos in place of the infant Zeus (485–486), and he swallows it unawares (487). This is the Greek form of the succession-myth device by which the doomed ruler is cheated of his supplanter. **Comparative apparatus (clearly labeled):** the stone-in-the-swallowing sequence and the whole 'kingship in heaven' succession pattern have close Near-Eastern analogues (the Hurro-Hittite Kumarbi cycle, where a stone figures in the swallowing/birth sequence); this convergence is recorded as comparative apparatus only and is not fused with any central glossary entry, per the signed-off Block-A/B non-fusion precedent. See the disgorged-stone note at 500 and the overlay entry `sema-stone-at-pytho-theogony`.

lines.text: Οὐρανίδῃ μέγʼ ἄνακτι, θεῶν προτέρῳ βασιλῆι.
lines.translit: Ouranidē meg' anakti theōn proterō basilēi

i18n.en: to the son of Ouranos, the great lord, the former king of the gods.

lines.text: τὸν τόθʼ ἑλὼν χείρεσσιν ἑὴν ἐσκάτθετο νηδὺν
lines.translit: ton toth' helōn cheiressin heēn eskattheto nēdyn

i18n.en: Then he took it in his hands and thrust it down into his belly,

lines.text: σχέτλιος· οὐδʼ ἐνόησε μετὰ φρεσίν, ὥς οἱ ὀπίσσω
lines.translit: schetlios oud' enoēse meta phresin hōs hoi opissō

i18n.en: the wretch; nor did he perceive in his heart that for the time to come

lines.text: ἀντὶ λίθου ἑὸς υἱὸς ἀνίκητος καὶ ἀκηδὴς
lines.translit: anti lithou heos hyios anikētos kai akēdēs

i18n.en: in place of the stone his own son, unconquered and untroubled,

lines.text: λείπεθʼ, ὅ μιν τάχʼ ἔμελλε βίῃ καὶ χερσὶ δαμάσσας
lines.translit: leipeth' ho min tach' emelle biē kai chersi damassas

i18n.en: was left behind, who soon by force and by his hands was to overcome him

lines.text: τιμῆς ἐξελάειν, ὃ δʼ ἐν ἀθανάτοισι ἀνάξειν.
lines.translit: timēs exelaein ho d' en athanatoisi anaxein

i18n.en: and drive him from his honour, and himself reign among the immortals.

lines.text: καρπαλίμως δʼ ἄρʼ ἔπειτα μένος καὶ φαίδιμα γυῖα
lines.translit: karpalimōs d' ar' epeita menos kai phaidima gyia

i18n.en: And swiftly thereafter the strength and glorious limbs

lines.text: ηὔξετο τοῖο ἄνακτος· ἐπιπλομένων δʼ ἐνιαυτῶν
lines.translit: ēuxeto toio anaktos epiplomenōn d' eniautōn

i18n.en: of that lord grew; and as the years rolled round,

lines.text: Γαίης ἐννεσίῃσι πολυφραδέεσσι δολωθεὶς
lines.translit: Gaiēs ennesiēsi polyphradeessi dolōtheis

i18n.en: beguiled by the shrewd promptings of Gaia,

lines.text: ὃν γόνον ἄψ ἀνέηκε μέγας Κρόνος ἀγκυλομήτης
lines.translit: hon gonon aps aneēke megas Kronos ankylomētēs

i18n.en: great Kronos of the crooked counsel brought up his offspring again,

lines.text: νικηθεὶς τέχνῃσι βίηφί τε παιδὸς ἑοῖο.
lines.translit: nikētheis technēsi biēphi te paidos heoio

i18n.en: overcome by the arts and the force of his own son.

notes.official: Line 496 (*νικηθεὶς τέχνῃσι βίηφί τε παιδὸς ἑοῖο*) is bracketed (athetized) in the edition; per the athetized-lines convention it is retained and translated unmarked in the surface, the athetesis recorded here. See `athetized-lines-convention-theogony`.

lines.text: πρῶτον δʼ ἐξέμεσεν λίθον, ὃν πύματον κατέπινεν·
lines.translit: prōton d' exemesen lithon hon pymaton katepinen

i18n.en: First he vomited up the stone, which he had swallowed last;

lines.text: τὸν μὲν Ζεὺς στήριξε κατὰ χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης
lines.translit: ton men Zeus stērixe kata chthonos euryodeiēs

i18n.en: and Zeus fixed it fast in the wide-wayed earth

lines.text: Πυθοῖ ἐν ἠγαθέῃ γυάλοις ὕπο Παρνησοῖο
lines.translit: Pythoi en ēgatheē gyalois hypo Parnēsoio

i18n.en: at holy Pytho, in the glens of Parnassos,

notes.official: Source spelling quirks preserved verbatim: *Παρνησοῖο* (with eta) is normalized to the standard 'Parnassos' in the surface, the source form kept in the text field; *Πυθοῖ* 'at Pytho' is the Greek form of the Delphic site. Governed by `place-name-greek-forms-block-c-theogony`.

lines.text: σῆμʼ ἔμεν ἐξοπίσω, θαῦμα θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν.
lines.translit: sēm' emen exopisō thauma thnētoisi brotoisin

i18n.en: to be a sign thereafter, a marvel to mortal men.

notes.official: The stone Kronos swallowed is vomited up first of all (497) and Zeus fixes it fast at Pytho, in the glens below Parnassos (498–499), *σῆμʼ ἔμεν ἐξοπίσω, θαῦμα θνητοῖσι βροτοῖσιν* 'to be a sign thereafter, a marvel to mortal men' (500). *σῆμα* 'sign, mark, marker, token' is rendered 'sign' with Evelyn-White; the text says only *σῆμα* and *θαῦμα* 'marvel'. **Lens-discipline / reception note:** the later identification of this Delphic stone as the *omphalos*, the 'navel-stone' marking the centre of the earth, is NOT in Hesiod — the word *ὀμφαλός* does not occur here — and that identification is later reception; it is kept out of the surface and named here only as clearly-labeled apparatus (cf. the central `jerusalem-as-omphalos` entries, which are not extended to this text). See `sema-stone-at-pytho-theogony` (resolving THEO-500).

lines.text: λῦσε δὲ πατροκασιγνήτους ὀλοῶν ὑπὸ δεσμῶν
lines.translit: lyse de patrokasignētous oloōn hypo desmōn

i18n.en: And he freed his father's brothers from their deadly bonds,

lines.text: Οὐρανίδας, οὓς δῆσε πατὴρ ἀεσιφροσύνῃσιν·
lines.translit: Ouranidas hous dēse patēr aesiphrosynēsin

i18n.en: the sons of Ouranos, whom their father had bound in his folly;

lines.text: οἳ οἱ ἀπεμνήσαντο χάριν ἐυεργεσιάων,
lines.translit: hoi hoi apemnēsanto charin euergesiaōn

i18n.en: and they remembered to repay him with gratitude for his kindness,

lines.text: δῶκαν δὲ βροντὴν ἠδʼ αἰθαλόεντα κεραυνὸν
lines.translit: dōkan de brontēn ēd' aithaloenta keraunon

i18n.en: and they gave him thunder and the blazing thunderbolt

notes.official: The Kyklopes, freed by Zeus from their bonds (501–502), repay him with the storm-triad *βροντή / (αἰθαλόεντα) κεραυνός / στεροπή* (504–505), rendered 'thunder / blazing thunderbolt / lightning' with Evelyn-White. The three-way sense — *brontē* the sound, *keraunos* the bolt/shaft, *steropē/asteropē* the flash — is not lexically rigid in the poem, and the same triad recurs in the Titanomachy at 690–691, 699 and 707 (and the single *brontē* at 458, *keraunos* at 515); it is rendered consistently across the block. See the overlay entry `thunder-triad-bronte-keraunos-sterope-theogony` (resolving THEO-504).

lines.text: καὶ στεροπήν· τὸ πρὶν δὲ πελώρη Γαῖα κεκεύθει·
lines.translit: kai steropēn to prin de pelōrē Gaia kekeuthei

i18n.en: and lightning; before this, huge Gaia had kept them hidden.

lines.text: τοῖς πίσυνος θνητοῖσι καὶ ἀθανάτοισιν ἀνάσσει.
lines.translit: tois pisynos thnētoisi kai athanatoisin anassei

i18n.en: Trusting in these he rules over mortals and immortals.

lines.text: κούρην δʼ Ἰαπετὸς καλλίσφυρον Ὠκεανίνην
lines.translit: kourēn d' Iapetos kallisphyron Ōkeaninēn

i18n.en: And Iapetos took to wife the fair-ankled maiden, daughter of Okeanos,

lines.text: ἠγάγετο Κλυμένην καὶ ὁμὸν λέχος εἰσανέβαινεν.
lines.translit: ēgageto Klymenēn kai homon lechos eisanebainen

i18n.en: Klymene, and went up into a common bed with her.

lines.text: ἣ δέ οἱ Ἄτλαντα κρατερόφρονα γείνατο παῖδα·
lines.translit: hē de hoi Atlanta kraterophrona geinato paida

i18n.en: And she bore him a stout-hearted son, Atlas;

lines.text: τίκτε δʼ ὑπερκύδαντα Μενοίτιον ἠδὲ Προμηθέα
lines.translit: tikte d' hyperkydanta Menoition ēde Promēthea

i18n.en: and she bore exceedingly proud Menoitios, and Prometheus,

lines.text: ποικίλον αἰολόμητιν, ἁμαρτίνοόν τʼ Ἐπιμηθέα
lines.translit: poikilon aiolomētin hamartinoon t' Epimēthea

i18n.en: subtle and crafty of counsel, and Epimetheus the blundering-minded,

notes.official: The Iapetids: Atlas, Menoitios, Prometheus and Epimetheus. Two speaking-names carry a pointed contrast left visible only in the Greek, per the folk-etymology convention (cf. the Titans, 207–210): *Προμηθεύς* 'fore-thinker' — here *ποικίλον αἰολόμητιν* 'subtle and shifting of counsel' — against *Ἐπιμηθεύς* 'after-thinker', glossed by *ἁμαρτίνοος* 'of erring mind' (511). The play (Prometheus foresees, Epimetheus learns too late) is not manufactured into an English pun; the epithets are rendered literally.

lines.text: ὃς κακὸν ἐξ ἀρχῆς γένετʼ ἀνδράσιν ἀλφηστῇσιν·
lines.translit: hos kakon ex archēs genet' andrasin alphēstēsin

i18n.en: who from the beginning was an evil to men who live by bread;

lines.text: πρῶτος γάρ ῥα Διὸς πλαστὴν ὑπέδεκτο γυναῖκα
lines.translit: prōtos gar rha Dios plastēn hypedekto gynaika

i18n.en: for he was the first to receive from Zeus the fashioned woman,

lines.text: παρθένον. ὑβριστὴν δὲ Μενοίτιον εὐρύοπα Ζεὺς
lines.translit: parthenon hybristēn de Menoition euryopa Zeus

i18n.en: the maiden. But wide-seeing Zeus sent the presumptuous Menoitios

lines.text: εἰς Ἔρεβος κατέπεμψε βαλὼν ψολόεντι κεραυνῷ
lines.translit: eis Erebos katepempse balōn psoloenti keraunō

i18n.en: down to Erebos, striking him with a smoking thunderbolt,

lines.text: εἵνεκʼ ἀτασθαλίης τε καὶ ἠνορέης ὑπερόπλου.
lines.translit: heinek' atasthaliēs te kai ēnoreēs hyperoplou

i18n.en: because of his reckless folly and his overweening manhood.

lines.text: Ἄτλας δʼ οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἔχει κρατερῆς ὑπʼ ἀνάγκης
lines.translit: Atlas d' ouranon euryn echei kraterēs hyp' anankēs

i18n.en: And Atlas holds the wide heaven under strong constraint,

lines.text: πείρασιν ἐν γαίης, πρόπαρ Εσπερίδων λιγυφώνων,
lines.translit: peirasin en gaiēs propar Esperidōn ligyphōnōn

i18n.en: at the bounds of the earth, before the clear-voiced Hesperides,

notes.official: Source quirk preserved verbatim: the edition prints *Εσπερίδων* unaccented and without the rough breathing at 518; the surface gives the standard 'Hesperides' (the clear-voiced daughters at the bounds of the earth), the source form kept in the text field.

lines.text: ἑστηὼς κεφαλῇ τε καὶ ἀκαμάτῃσι χέρεσσιν·
lines.translit: hestēōs kephalē te kai akamatēsi cheressin

i18n.en: standing, with his head and unwearying hands;

lines.text: ταύτην γάρ οἱ μοῖραν ἐδάσσατο μητίετα Ζεύς.
lines.translit: tautēn gar hoi moiran edassato mētieta Zeus

i18n.en: for this is the portion that Zeus the counsellor allotted to him.

notes.official: Atlas holds the wide heaven (517) as *ταύτην … μοῖραν … ἐδάσσατο* 'this portion Zeus allotted to him' (520). Here *μοῖρα* 'portion/lot' and the division-verb *δατέομαι* belong to the fate-allotment / meat-division domain, distinct from the divine-prerogative apportionment governed by the honour-vocabulary entry; the two are kept apart (see on 535). Rendered 'portion … allotted' with Evelyn-White; governed by `dasmos-moira-meat-division-mekone-theogony`.

lines.text: δῆσε δʼ ἀλυκτοπέδῃσι Προμηθέα ποικιλόβουλον
lines.translit: dēse d' alyktopedēsi Promēthea poikiloboulon

i18n.en: And he bound crafty-counselled Prometheus with inescapable fetters,

notes.official: The Prometheus-punishment digression (521–534) is placed here by ring-composition before the Mekone/​fire aetiology that explains it (535 ff). *ἀλυκτοπέδῃσι* 'inescapable fetters' bind him to a pillar; the long-winged eagle eats his ever-regrowing immortal liver (523–525) until Herakles slays it (526–528), 'not without the will of Olympian Zeus' (529), so that Herakles' glory might grow (530–531). Rendered with Evelyn-White; no divergence.

lines.text: δεσμοῖς ἀργαλέοισι μέσον διὰ κίονʼ ἐλάσσας·
lines.translit: desmois argaleoisi meson dia kion' elassas

i18n.en: grievous bonds, driving them through the middle of a pillar;

lines.text: καί οἱ ἐπʼ αἰετὸν ὦρσε τανύπτερον· αὐτὰρ ὅ γʼ ἧπαρ
lines.translit: kai hoi ep' aieton ōrse tanypteron autar ho g' hēpar

i18n.en: and he set upon him a long-winged eagle; and it kept eating

lines.text: ἤσθιεν ἀθάνατον, τὸ δʼ ἀέξετο ἶσον ἁπάντη
lines.translit: ēsthien athanaton to d' aexeto ison hapantē

i18n.en: his immortal liver, which grew again to full as much on every side

lines.text: νυκτός ὅσον πρόπαν ἦμαρ ἔδοι τανυσίπτερος ὄρνις.
lines.translit: nyktos hoson propan ēmar edoi tanysipteros ornis

i18n.en: by night as the long-winged bird had eaten in the whole day.

lines.text: τὸν μὲν ἄρʼ Ἀλκμήνης καλλισφύρου ἄλκιμος υἱὸς
lines.translit: ton men ar' Alkmēnēs kallisphyrou alkimos hyios

i18n.en: That bird the valiant son of fair-ankled Alkmene,

lines.text: Ἡρακλέης ἔκτεινε, κακὴν δʼ ἀπὸ νοῦσον ἄλαλκεν
lines.translit: Hērakleēs ekteine kakēn d' apo nouson alalken

i18n.en: Herakles, slew; and he warded off the cruel plague

lines.text: Ἰαπετιονίδῃ καὶ ἐλύσατο δυσφροσυνάων
lines.translit: Iapetionidē kai elysato dysphrosynaōn

i18n.en: from the son of Iapetos, and freed him from his torments,

lines.text: οὐκ ἀέκητι Ζηνὸς Ὀλυμπίου ὑψιμέδοντος,
lines.translit: ouk aekēti Zēnos Olympiou hypsimedontos

i18n.en: not without the will of Olympian Zeus who reigns on high,

lines.text: ὄφρʼ Ἡρακλῆος Θηβαγενέος κλέος εἴη
lines.translit: ophr' Hēraklēos Thēbageneos kleos eiē

i18n.en: so that the glory of Theban-born Herakles might be

lines.text: πλεῖον ἔτʼ ἢ τὸ πάροιθεν ἐπὶ χθόνα πουλυβότειραν.
lines.translit: pleion et' ē to paroithen epi chthona poulyboteiran

i18n.en: yet greater than before over the bounteous earth.

lines.text: ταῦτʼ ἄρα ἁζόμενος τίμα ἀριδείκετον υἱόν·
lines.translit: taut' ara hazomenos tima arideiketon hyion

i18n.en: Revering this, he honoured his renowned son;

lines.text: καί περ χωόμενος παύθη χόλου, ὃν πρὶν ἔχεσκεν,
lines.translit: kai per chōomenos pauthē cholou hon prin echesken

i18n.en: and, though angered, he ceased from the wrath which he had before,

lines.text: οὕνεκʼ ἐρίζετο βουλὰς ὑπερμενέι Κρονίωνι.
lines.translit: hounek' erizeto boulas hypermenei Kroniōni

i18n.en: because Prometheus had matched his wits against the exceedingly mighty son of Kronos.

lines.text: καὶ γὰρ ὅτʼ ἐκρίνοντο θεοὶ θνητοί τʼ ἄνθρωποι
lines.translit: kai gar hot' ekrinonto theoi thnētoi t' anthrōpoi

i18n.en: For when the gods and mortal men were settling their reckoning

notes.official: The Mekone episode (535–544), aetiology of Greek animal sacrifice. *ἐκρίνοντο* (535) is itself ambiguous — 'were settling their reckoning / had a dispute' (Evelyn-White, followed here) versus 'were being separated', i.e. the parting of gods and men (West 1966, noted but not adopted). Prometheus divides (*δασσάμενος*, 537) the ox into two *μοῖραι* (544), hiding the good meat under the paunch and the bare bones under glistening fat. The *δα-* division-verbs and *μοῖρα* here are the meat-division / fate-allotment domain, held distinct from the divine-prerogative *timē/geras* apportionment of the Hekate hymn; the honour-vocabulary entry is therefore NOT applied. See `dasmos-moira-meat-division-mekone-theogony` (resolving THEO-536). **Comparative apparatus (labeled):** the 'why the gods get the smoke and bones, men the meat' aetiology is a Greek instance of a wider Near-Eastern sacrificial-portion trope; the link is apparatus only and is not fused with the central flood-sacrifice/​aroma entries, per the non-fusion precedent.

lines.text: Μηκώνῃ, τότʼ ἔπειτα μέγαν βοῦν πρόφρονι θυμῷ
lines.translit: Mēkōnē tot' epeita megan boun prophroni thymō

i18n.en: at Mekone, then with a ready heart he portioned out a great ox

lines.text: δασσάμενος προέθηκε, Διὸς νόον ἐξαπαφίσκων.
lines.translit: dassamenos proethēke Dios noon exapaphiskōn

i18n.en: and set it before them, seeking to beguile the mind of Zeus.

lines.text: τοῖς μὲν γὰρ σάρκας τε καὶ ἔγκατα πίονα δημῷ
lines.translit: tois men gar sarkas te kai enkata piona dēmō

i18n.en: For on the one side he put the flesh and the entrails rich with fat

lines.text: ἐν ῥινῷ κατέθηκε καλύψας γαστρὶ βοείῃ,
lines.translit: en rhinō katethēke kalypsas gastri boeiē

i18n.en: within the hide, covering it with the ox's paunch;

lines.text: τῷ δʼ αὖτʼ ὀστέα λευκὰ βοὸς δολίῃ ἐπὶ τέχνῃ
lines.translit: tō d' aut' ostea leuka boos doliē epi technē

i18n.en: but on the other he laid out the white bones of the ox with cunning craft,

lines.text: εὐθετίσας κατέθηκε καλύψας ἀργέτι δημῷ.
lines.translit: euthetisas katethēke kalypsas argeti dēmō

i18n.en: arranging them well, and covered them with shining fat.

lines.text: δὴ τότε μιν προσέειπε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε·
lines.translit: dē tote min proseeipe patēr andrōn te theōn te

i18n.en: Then the father of men and gods addressed him:

lines.text: Ἰαπετιονίδη, πάντων ἀριδείκετʼ ἀνάκτων,
lines.translit: Iapetionidē pantōn arideiket' anaktōn

i18n.en: “Son of Iapetos, most glorious of all lords,

lines.text: ὦ πέπον, ὡς ἑτεροζήλως διεδάσσαο μοίρας.
lines.translit: ō pepon hōs heterozēlōs diedassao moiras

i18n.en: my friend, how one-sidedly you have divided the portions!”

lines.text: ὣς φάτο κερτομέων Ζεὺς ἄφθιτα μήδεα εἰδώς.
lines.translit: hōs phato kertomeōn Zeus aphthita mēdea eidōs

i18n.en: So spoke in mockery Zeus, who knows imperishable counsels.

lines.text: τὸν δʼ αὖτε προσέειπε Προμηθεὺς ἀγκυλομήτης
lines.translit: ton d' aute proseeipe Promētheus ankylomētēs

i18n.en: Then Prometheus of the crooked counsel answered him,

notes.official: *ἀγκυλομήτης* 'of crooked counsel' — Kronos's signature epithet (18, 137, 168, and in Block C at 473 and 495) — is here transferred by Hesiod to Prometheus. The lexical value is identical, so the rendering 'of the crooked counsel' is unchanged; the point is that Hesiod marks Prometheus as the succession's new crooked-counsellor set against Zeus. The Kronos-scoped entry `ankylometes-crooked-counsel-kronos-epithet-theogony` is deliberately NOT applied at 546 — its scope is Kronos — and the epithet-transfer is recorded here as a distinct decision (resolving THEO-546).

lines.text: ἦκʼ ἐπιμειδήσας, δολίης δʼ οὐ λήθετο τέχνης·
lines.translit: ēk' epimeidēsas doliēs d' ou lētheto technēs

i18n.en: smiling softly, and he did not forget his cunning craft:

lines.text: ζεῦ κύδιστε μέγιστε θεῶν αἰειγενετάων,
lines.translit: zeu kydiste megiste theōn aieigenetaōn

i18n.en: “Zeus, most glorious and greatest of the eternal gods,

lines.text: τῶν δʼ ἕλεʼ, ὁπποτέρην σε ἐνὶ φρεσὶ θυμὸς ἀνώγει.
lines.translit: tōn d' hele' hoppoterēn se eni phresi thymos anōgei

i18n.en: choose of these whichever the heart within your breast bids you.”

lines.text: Φῆ ῥα δολοφρονέων· Ζεὺς δʼ ἄφθιτα μήδεα εἰδὼς
lines.translit: Phē rha dolophroneōn Zeus d' aphthita mēdea eidōs

i18n.en: So he spoke with crafty intent; but Zeus, who knows imperishable counsels,

lines.text: γνῶ ῥʼ οὐδʼ ἠγνοίησε δόλον· κακὰ δʼ ὄσσετο θυμῷ
lines.translit: gnō rh' oud' ēgnoiēse dolon kaka d' osseto thymō

i18n.en: knew the trick and did not fail to see it; and he foresaw in his heart evils

lines.text: θνητοῖς ἀνθρώποισι, τὰ καὶ τελέεσθαι ἔμελλεν.
lines.translit: thnētois anthrōpoisi ta kai teleesthai emellen

i18n.en: for mortal men, which were also to be brought to pass.

lines.text: χερσὶ δʼ ὅ γʼ ἀμφοτέρῃσιν ἀνείλετο λευκὸν ἄλειφαρ.
lines.translit: chersi d' ho g' amphoterēsin aneileto leukon aleiphar

i18n.en: With both his hands he took up the white fat.

lines.text: χώσατο δὲ φρένας ἀμφί, χόλος δέ μιν ἵκετο θυμόν,
lines.translit: chōsato de phrenas amphi cholos de min hiketo thymon

i18n.en: And he was angered in his heart, and wrath came upon his spirit,

lines.text: ὡς ἴδεν ὀστέα λευκὰ βοὸς δολίῃ ἐπὶ τέχνῃ.
lines.translit: hōs iden ostea leuka boos doliē epi technē

i18n.en: when he saw the white bones of the ox laid out with cunning craft.

lines.text: ἐκ τοῦ δʼ ἀθανάτοισιν ἐπὶ χθονὶ φῦλʼ ἀνθρώπων
lines.translit: ek tou d' athanatoisin epi chthoni phyl' anthrōpōn

i18n.en: And from that time the tribes of men upon the earth

notes.official: *ἐκ τοῦ* 'from that time' men burn the white bones on fragrant altars (556–557): the aetiological close of the Mekone division (see on 535). No divergence from Evelyn-White.

lines.text: καίουσʼ ὀστέα λευκὰ θυηέντων ἐπὶ βωμῶν.
lines.translit: kaious' ostea leuka thyēentōn epi bōmōn

i18n.en: burn white bones to the immortals upon fragrant altars.

lines.text: τὸν δὲ μέγʼ ὀχθήσας προσέφη νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς·
lines.translit: ton de meg' ochthēsas prosephē nephelēgereta Zeus

i18n.en: But greatly vexed, Zeus the cloud-gatherer said to him:

lines.text: Ἰαπετιονίδη, πάντων πέρι μήδεα εἰδώς,
lines.translit: Iapetionidē pantōn peri mēdea eidōs

i18n.en: “Son of Iapetos, knowing counsels beyond all others,

lines.text: ὦ πέπον, οὐκ ἄρα πω δολίης ἐπιλήθεο τέχνης.
lines.translit: ō pepon ouk ara pō doliēs epilētheo technēs

i18n.en: my friend, so you have not yet forgotten your cunning craft!”

lines.text: ὣς φάτο χωόμενος Ζεὺς ἄφθιτα μήδεα εἰδώς·
lines.translit: hōs phato chōomenos Zeus aphthita mēdea eidōs

i18n.en: So spoke in anger Zeus, who knows imperishable counsels;

lines.text: ἐκ τούτου δὴ ἔπειτα δόλου μεμνημένος αἰεὶ
lines.translit: ek toutou dē epeita dolou memnēmenos aiei

i18n.en: and from that time, ever mindful of the trick,

lines.text: οὐκ ἐδίδου Μελίῃσι πυρὸς μένος ἀκαμάτοιο
lines.translit: ouk edidou Meliēsi pyros menos akamatoio

i18n.en: he would not give the might of unwearying fire to the Meliai,

notes.official: Two cruxes in the fire-theft. First, *Μελίῃσι* (563): the dative plural 'to the Meliai'. Evelyn-White takes it as the *Melian race* of mortal men, in apposition to *θνητοῖς ἀνθρώποις* 'mortal men' (564) and connected to the ash-tree nymphs Meliai born from Ouranos's blood (187; cf. the ash-tree origin of the bronze race in *Works and Days*); alternatives read a bare literal 'ash-trees' or emend to *μελέῃσι* 'to wretched (mortals)'. The transmitted text and the apposition-reading are followed; because this commits to one construal of a genuine crux, the overlay entry `meliai-crux-theogony` is marked `inferred` (resolving THEO-563). Second, the fire itself: see on 566–567 and `fire-theft-prometheus-theogony`.

lines.text: θνητοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οἳ ἐπὶ χθονὶ ναιετάουσιν.
lines.translit: thnētois anthrōpois hoi epi chthoni naietaousin

i18n.en: to mortal men who dwell upon the earth.

lines.text: ἀλλά μιν ἐξαπάτησεν ἐὺς πάις Ἰαπετοῖο
lines.translit: alla min exapatēsen eus pais Iapetoio

i18n.en: But the good son of Iapetos deceived him,

lines.text: κλέψας ἀκαμάτοιο πυρὸς τηλέσκοπον. αὐγὴν
lines.translit: klepsas akamatoio pyros tēleskopon augēn

i18n.en: having stolen the far-seen gleam of unwearying fire

notes.official: The fire-theft. Prometheus steals the *τηλέσκοπον αὐγήν* 'far-seen gleam' of unwearying fire and carries it *ἐν κοΐλῳ νάρθηκι* 'in a hollow fennel-stalk' (567) — the giant fennel, *Ferula communis*, whose dry pith carries a smouldering ember; Evelyn-White's 'hollow fennel-stalk' is retained over a transliterated 'narthex' or a generic 'reed' (resolving THEO-567). Source quirk preserved verbatim: the edition prints a period after *τηλέσκοπον* mid-phrase (*κλέψας … τηλέσκοπον. αὐγὴν*), the sense enjambing into 567. See `fire-theft-prometheus-theogony`. **Lens-discipline note:** the Promethean fire as culture- and knowledge-gift to humanity is a Wheel-of-Heaven-resonant theme, but the line says only 'fire'; the reading is confined to this apparatus and no central fire/knowledge entry is invoked (none exists).

lines.text: ἐν κοΐλῳ νάρθηκι· δάκεν δέ ἑ νειόθι θυμόν,
lines.translit: en koilō narthēki daken de he neiothi thymon

i18n.en: in a hollow fennel-stalk; and it stung him to the depths of his heart,

notes.official: See on 566: *νάρθηξ* 'fennel-stalk' (the giant fennel, ember-carrier of the fire-theft).

lines.text: Ζῆνʼ ὑψιβρεμέτην, ἐχόλωσε δέ μιν φίλον ἦτορ,
lines.translit: Zēn' hypsibremetēn echolōse de min philon ētor

i18n.en: Zeus who thunders on high, and it angered his dear heart

lines.text: ὡς ἴδʼ ἐν ἀνθρώποισι πυρὸς τηλέσκοπον αὐγήν.
lines.translit: hōs id' en anthrōpoisi pyros tēleskopon augēn

i18n.en: when he saw among men the far-seen gleam of fire.

lines.text: αὐτίκα δʼ ἀντὶ πυρὸς τεῦξεν κακὸν ἀνθρώποισιν·
lines.translit: autika d' anti pyros teuxen kakon anthrōpoisin

i18n.en: At once he made an evil for men in return for the fire:

lines.text: γαίης γὰρ σύμπλασσε περικλυτὸς Ἀμφιγυήεις
lines.translit: gaiēs gar symplasse periklytos Amphigyēeis

i18n.en: for the renowned Lame One moulded from earth

notes.official: *περικλυτὸς Ἀμφιγυήεις* 'the renowned Lame One' (571, 579) designates Hephaestus, who is not named here; the epithet-title is rendered literally and the proper name is not substituted (Evelyn-White). The smith-god moulds the first woman *γαίης* 'from earth', a likeness of a modest maiden, 'through the plans of the son of Kronos' (572). See `periphrastic-title-unnamed-god-theogony` (resolving the Amphigyeeis half of THEO-571). **Lens-discipline note:** the fashioning of humankind's counterpart from earth by a craftsman-god is a WoH-salient motif; the note names the smith and stays at that level, pressing no cosmological reading.

lines.text: παρθένῳ αἰδοίῃ ἴκελον Κρονίδεω διὰ βουλάς.
lines.translit: parthenō aidoiē ikelon Kronideō dia boulas

i18n.en: the likeness of a modest maiden, through the plans of the son of Kronos.

lines.text: ζῶσε δὲ καὶ κόσμησε θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη
lines.translit: zōse de kai kosmēse thea glaukōpis Athēnē

i18n.en: And the bright-eyed goddess Athena girded and adorned her

lines.text: ἀργυφέη ἐσθῆτι· κατὰ κρῆθεν δὲ καλύπτρην
lines.translit: argypheē esthēti kata krēthen de kalyptrēn

i18n.en: in silvery raiment; and down from her head she spread with her hands

lines.text: δαιδαλέην χείρεσσι κατέσχεθε, θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι·
lines.translit: daidaleēn cheiressi kateschethe thauma idesthai

i18n.en: an embroidered veil, a wonder to behold;

lines.text: ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ στεφάνους, νεοθηλέος ἄνθεα ποίης,
lines.translit: amphi de hoi stephanous neothēleos anthea poiēs

i18n.en: and about her head garlands, the flowers of fresh-blooming grass,

notes.official: Lines 576–577 (the garland couplet, *ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ στεφάνους … Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη*) are bracketed (athetized) in the edition; per the athetized-lines convention they are retained and translated unmarked in the surface, the athetesis recorded here. See `athetized-lines-convention-theogony`.

lines.text: ἱμερτοὺς περίθηκε καρήατι Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη.
lines.translit: himertous perithēke karēati Pallas Athēnē

i18n.en: lovely ones, Pallas Athena set upon her head.

lines.text: ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ στεφάνην χρυσέην κεφαλῆφιν ἔθηκε,
lines.translit: amphi de hoi stephanēn chryseēn kephalēphin ethēke

i18n.en: And about her head she set a crown of gold,

lines.text: τὴν αὐτὸς ποίησε περικλυτὸς Ἀμφιγυήεις
lines.translit: tēn autos poiēse periklytos Amphigyēeis

i18n.en: which the renowned Lame One himself had made,

lines.text: ἀσκήσας παλάμῃσι, χαριζόμενος Διὶ πατρί.
lines.translit: askēsas palamēsi charizomenos Dii patri

i18n.en: working it with his hands, to please Zeus his father.

lines.text: τῇ δʼ ἐνὶ δαίδαλα πολλὰ τετεύχατο, θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι,
lines.translit: tē d' eni daidala polla teteuchato thauma idesthai

i18n.en: On it were wrought many curious things, a wonder to behold,

lines.text: κνώδαλʼ, ὅσʼ ἤπειρος πολλὰ τρέφει ἠδὲ θάλασσα,
lines.translit: knōdal' hos' ēpeiros polla trephei ēde thalassa

i18n.en: wild beasts, such as the land and the sea nourish in multitudes;

lines.text: τῶν ὅ γε πόλλʼ ἐνέθηκε,—χάρις δʼ ἀπελάμπετο πολλή,—
lines.translit: tōn ho ge poll' enethēkecharis d' apelampeto pollē

i18n.en: many of these he set there,—and great grace shone from it,—

lines.text: θαυμάσια, ζῴοισιν ἐοικότα φωνήεσσιν.
lines.translit: thaumasia zōoisin eoikota phōnēessin

i18n.en: marvellous things, like living creatures that have voice.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ δὴ τεῦξε καλὸν κακὸν ἀντʼ ἀγαθοῖο.
lines.translit: autar epei dē teuxe kalon kakon ant' agathoio

i18n.en: But when he had made the beautiful evil in exchange for the good,

notes.official: *καλὸν κακόν* 'the beautiful evil' (585): the oxymoron is preserved with Evelyn-White. Crucial discipline — the *Theogony* neither names Pandora nor mentions any jar (*pithos*): the woman here is only the *πλαστὴ γυνή* 'fashioned woman' (513) / *παρθένος* moulded by Hephaestus and adorned by Athena; the name 'Pandora' and the jar belong to *Works and Days*, and none of that material is imported (resolving THEO-585). Source quirk preserved verbatim: the edition prints a line-final period at 585 though the sentence enjambs into 586 (*ἐξάγαγʼ* 'he led her out'). See `kalon-kakon-fashioned-woman-theogony`. **Comparative apparatus (labeled):** the woman-as-fashioned-bane aetiology invites comparison with the Genesis 2–3 creation-of-woman/​Eve tradition; the comparison is apparatus only and is not fused with any central Eve entry (`ish-ishah`, `ezer-kenegdo`), per the non-fusion precedent.

lines.text: ἐξάγαγʼ, ἔνθα περ ἄλλοι ἔσαν θεοὶ ἠδʼ ἄνθρωποι,
lines.translit: exagag' entha per alloi esan theoi ēd' anthrōpoi

i18n.en: he led her out where the other gods and men were,

lines.text: κόσμῳ ἀγαλλομένην γλαυκώπιδος ὀβριμοπάτρης.
lines.translit: kosmō agallomenēn glaukōpidos obrimopatrēs

i18n.en: exulting in the adornment of the bright-eyed daughter of a mighty father.

lines.text: θαῦμα δʼ ἔχʼ ἀθανάτους τε θεοὺς θνητούς τʼ ἀνθρώπους,
lines.translit: thauma d' ech' athanatous te theous thnētous t' anthrōpous

i18n.en: And wonder held the immortal gods and mortal men

lines.text: ὡς εἶδον δόλον αἰπύν, ἀμήχανον ἀνθρώποισιν.
lines.translit: hōs eidon dolon aipyn amēchanon anthrōpoisin

i18n.en: when they saw the sheer deception, irresistible to men.

lines.text: ἐκ τῆς γὰρ γένος ἐστὶ γυναικῶν θηλυτεράων,
lines.translit: ek tēs gar genos esti gynaikōn thēlyteraōn

i18n.en: For from her is the race of women, the female kind;

notes.official: *ἐκ τῆς γὰρ γένος ἐστὶ γυναικῶν* 'for from her is the race of women' (590): the aetiology derives womankind as a *πῆμα* 'plague, bane' for men (592), with the drone-and-bee simile (594–599) and the marriage-dilemma (600–612). It is rendered literally, without softening (resolving THEO-590). **Register note:** this is an ancient misogynistic aetiology; accuracy-before-lens keeps the source's sense intact — the translation neither endorses nor sanitizes it, and the register is flagged here as a datum of the text, not editorialized in the surface. Governed by `kalon-kakon-fashioned-woman-theogony`.

lines.text: τῆς γὰρ ὀλώιόν ἐστι γένος καὶ φῦλα γυναικῶν,
lines.translit: tēs gar olōion esti genos kai phyla gynaikōn

i18n.en: from her is the deadly race and the tribes of women,

notes.official: Line 591 (*τῆς γὰρ ὀλώιόν ἐστι γένος καὶ φῦλα γυναικῶν*) is bracketed (athetized) in the edition as a doublet of 590; per the athetized-lines convention it is retained and translated unmarked in the surface, the athetesis recorded here. See `athetized-lines-convention-theogony`.

lines.text: πῆμα μέγʼ αἳ θνητοῖσι μετʼ ἀνδράσι ναιετάουσιν
lines.translit: pēma meg' hai thnētoisi met' andrasi naietaousin

i18n.en: a great plague, who dwell among mortal men,

lines.text: οὐλομένης πενίης οὐ σύμφοροι, ἀλλὰ κόροιο.
lines.translit: oulomenēs peniēs ou symphoroi alla koroio

i18n.en: no helpmeets in accursed poverty, but only in plenty.

lines.text: ὡς δʼ ὁπότʼ ἐν σμήνεσσι κατηρεφέεσσι μέλισσαι
lines.translit: hōs d' hopot' en smēnessi katērepheessi melissai

i18n.en: And as when in roofed hives the bees

lines.text: κηφῆνας βόσκωσι, κακῶν ξυνήονας ἔργων—
lines.translit: kēphēnas boskōsi kakōn xynēonas ergōn

i18n.en: feed the drones, partners in evil works—

lines.text: αἳ μέν τε πρόπαν ἦμαρ ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα
lines.translit: hai men te propan ēmar es ēelion katadynta

i18n.en: the bees all day long until the sun goes down

lines.text: ἠμάτιαι σπεύδουσι τιθεῖσί τε κηρία λευκά,
lines.translit: ēmatiai speudousi titheisi te kēria leuka

i18n.en: busy themselves by day and lay the white combs,

lines.text: οἳ δʼ ἔντοσθε μένοντες ἐπηρεφέας κατὰ σίμβλους
lines.translit: hoi d' entosthe menontes epērepheas kata simblous

i18n.en: while the drones, staying within the roofed hives,

lines.text: ἀλλότριον κάματον σφετέρην ἐς γαστέρʼ ἀμῶνται—
lines.translit: allotrion kamaton spheterēn es gaster' amōntai

i18n.en: reap the labour of others into their own bellies—

lines.text: ὣς δʼ αὔτως ἄνδρεσσι κακὸν θνητοῖσι γυναῖκας
lines.translit: hōs d' autōs andressi kakon thnētoisi gynaikas

i18n.en: even so, as an evil for mortal men, did Zeus who thunders on high

lines.text: Ζεὺς ὑψιβρεμέτης θῆκεν, ξυνήονας ἔργων
lines.translit: Zeus hypsibremetēs thēken xynēonas ergōn

i18n.en: make women, partners in grievous works;

lines.text: ἀργαλέων· ἕτερον δὲ πόρεν κακὸν ἀντʼ ἀγαθοῖο·
lines.translit: argaleōn heteron de poren kakon ant' agathoio

i18n.en: and he gave a second evil in exchange for a good:

lines.text: ὅς κε γάμον φεύγων καὶ μέρμερα ἔργα γυναικῶν
lines.translit: hos ke gamon pheugōn kai mermera erga gynaikōn

i18n.en: whoever, shunning marriage and the troublesome works of women,

lines.text: μὴ γῆμαι ἐθέλῃ, ὀλοὸν δʼ ἐπὶ γῆρας ἵκοιτο
lines.translit: mē gēmai ethelē oloon d' epi gēras hikoito

i18n.en: is unwilling to wed, and comes to deadly old age

lines.text: χήτεϊ γηροκόμοιο· ὅ γʼ οὐ βιότου ἐπιδευὴς
lines.translit: chētei gērokomoio ho g' ou biotou epideuēs

i18n.en: with none to tend his age; he does not lack for livelihood

lines.text: ζώει, ἀποφθιμένου δὲ διὰ κτῆσιν δατέονται
lines.translit: zōei apophthimenou de dia ktēsin dateontai

i18n.en: while he lives, but when he dies his kinsmen divide his possessions

lines.text: χηρωσταί· ᾧ δʼ αὖτε γάμου μετὰ μοῖρα γένηται,
lines.translit: chērōstai hō d' aute gamou meta moira genētai

i18n.en: among themselves. And again, to whomever the lot of marriage falls,

lines.text: κεδνὴν δʼ ἔσχεν ἄκοιτιν ἀρηρυῖαν πραπίδεσσι,
lines.translit: kednēn d' eschen akoitin arēryian prapidessi

i18n.en: and he gets a good wife, fitted to his mind,

lines.text: τῷ δέ τʼ ἀπʼ αἰῶνος κακὸν ἐσθλῷ ἀντιφερίζει
lines.translit: tō de t' ap' aiōnos kakon esthlō antipherizei

i18n.en: for him throughout his life evil continually contends with good;

lines.text: ἐμμενές· ὃς δέ κε τέτμῃ ἀταρτηροῖο γενέθλης,
lines.translit: emmenes hos de ke tetmē atartēroio genethlēs

i18n.en: but whoever obtains the baneful sort

lines.text: ζώει ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἔχων ἀλίαστον ἀνίην
lines.translit: zōei eni stēthessin echōn aliaston aniēn

i18n.en: lives with unceasing pain in his breast,

lines.text: θυμῷ καὶ κραδίῃ, καὶ ἀνήκεστον κακόν ἐστιν.
lines.translit: thymō kai kradiē kai anēkeston kakon estin

i18n.en: in heart and spirit, and it is an evil past cure.

lines.text: ὣς οὐκ ἔστι Διὸς κλέψαι νόον οὐδὲ παρελθεῖν.
lines.translit: hōs ouk esti Dios klepsai noon oude parelthein

i18n.en: Thus it is not possible to deceive or to overreach the mind of Zeus;

lines.text: οὐδὲ γὰρ Ἰαπετιονίδης ἀκάκητα Προμηθεὺς
lines.translit: oude gar Iapetionidēs akakēta Promētheus

i18n.en: for not even Iapetos' son, kindly Prometheus,

notes.official: *ἀκάκητα Προμηθεύς* 'kindly / guileless Prometheus' (614): the epithet stands in pointed contrast to the *ἀγκυλομήτης* 'crooked-counselled' of 546 — even the guileless one could not escape Zeus's mind (613 'it is not possible to deceive or overreach the mind of Zeus'). Rendered with Evelyn-White.

lines.text: τοῖό γʼ ὑπεξήλυξε βαρὺν χόλον, ἀλλʼ ὑπʼ ἀνάγκης
lines.translit: toio g' hypexēlyxe baryn cholon all' hyp' anankēs

i18n.en: escaped his heavy wrath, but by necessity

lines.text: καὶ πολύιδριν ἐόντα μέγας κατὰ δεσμὸς ἐρύκει.
lines.translit: kai polyidrin eonta megas kata desmos erykei

i18n.en: a great bond holds him fast, for all his cunning.

lines.text: Βριάρεῳ δʼ ὡς πρῶτα πατὴρ ὠδύσσατο θυμῷ
lines.translit: Briareō d' hōs prōta patēr ōdyssato thymō

i18n.en: But when their father first grew angry in his heart at Briareos,

notes.official: *Βριάρεῳ* 'Briareos' (also 714; and the doublet *Ὀβριάρεως* at 734, see there): the transition to the Hundred-Handers, whom their father Ouranos had bound out of grudging fear of their strength, form and size (619–620) and imprisoned beneath the earth — setting up their release as Zeus's decisive allies in the Titanomachy (624–663). Governed by `theogony-name-and-title-conventions`.

lines.text: Κόττῳ τʼ ἠδὲ Γύῃ, δῆσεν κρατερῷ ἐνὶ δεσμῷ
lines.translit: Kottō t' ēde Gyē dēsen kraterō eni desmō

i18n.en: and at Kottos and Gyes, he bound them in a strong bond,

lines.text: ἠνορέην ὑπέροπλον ἀγώμενος ἠδὲ καὶ εἶδος
lines.translit: ēnoreēn hyperoplon agōmenos ēde kai eidos

i18n.en: grudging their overweening manhood and their form

lines.text: καὶ μέγεθος· κατένασσε δʼ ὑπὸ χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης.
lines.translit: kai megethos katenasse d' hypo chthonos euryodeiēs

i18n.en: and their size; and he made them dwell beneath the wide-wayed earth.

lines.text: ἔνθʼ οἵ γʼ ἄλγεʼ ἔχοντες ὑπὸ χθονὶ ναιετάοντες
lines.translit: enth' hoi g' alge' echontes hypo chthoni naietaontes

i18n.en: There they dwelt in pain, dwelling beneath the earth,

lines.text: εἵατʼ ἐπʼ ἐσχατιῇ, μεγάλης ἐν πείρασι γαίης,
lines.translit: heiat' ep' eschatiē megalēs en peirasi gaiēs

i18n.en: seated at the farthest edge, at the bounds of the great earth,

lines.text: δηθὰ μάλʼ ἀχνύμενοι, κραδίῃ μέγα πένθος ἔχοντες.
lines.translit: dētha mal' achnymenoi kradiē mega penthos echontes

i18n.en: grieving long, holding great sorrow in their hearts.

lines.text: ἀλλά σφεας Κρονίδης τε καὶ ἀθάνατοι θεοὶ ἄλλοι,
lines.translit: alla spheas Kronidēs te kai athanatoi theoi alloi

i18n.en: But the son of Kronos and the other immortal gods,

lines.text: οὓς τέκεν ἠύκομος Ῥείη Κρόνου ἐν φιλότητι,
lines.translit: hous teken ēukomos Rheiē Kronou en philotēti

i18n.en: whom fair-haired Rhea bore in love with Kronos,

lines.text: Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσιν ἀνήγαγον ἐς φάος αὖτις·
lines.translit: Gaiēs phradmosynēsin anēgagon es phaos autis

i18n.en: by the counsels of Gaia brought them up again to the light;

notes.official: *Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσιν* 'by the counsels of Gaia' (626): Gaia counsels the Olympians to bring the Hundred-Handers back up to the light (626) as the allies who will win them victory and glorious renown (627–628). This is the fourth link in the Gaia counsel/prophecy motif (463/475/494/626; see on 463), rendered literally with Evelyn-White. Governed by `gaia-counsel-prophecy-vocabulary-theogony`.

lines.text: αὐτὴ γάρ σφιν ἅπαντα διηνεκέως κατέλεξε
lines.translit: autē gar sphin hapanta diēnekeōs katelexe

i18n.en: for she herself told them everything from beginning to end,

lines.text: σὺν κείνοις νίκην τε καὶ ἀγλαὸν εὖχος ἀρέσθαι.
lines.translit: syn keinois nikēn te kai aglaon euchos aresthai

i18n.en: how with their help they would win victory and glorious renown.

lines.text: δηρὸν γὰρ μάρναντο πόνον θυμαλγέʼ ἔχοντες
lines.translit: dēron gar marnanto ponon thymalge' echontes

i18n.en: For long they had fought, enduring heart-grieving toil,

lines.text: Τιτῆνές τε θεοὶ καὶ ὅσοι Κρόνου ἐξεγένοντο,
lines.translit: Titēnes te theoi kai hosoi Kronou exegenonto

i18n.en: the Titan gods and all who were born of Kronos,

notes.official: The Titanomachy proem. *Τιτῆνές τε θεοὶ καὶ ὅσοι Κρόνου ἐξεγένοντο* (630; the formula recurs at 668, and at 648 in the first-person form *ἐκγενόμεσθα*) names both armies in apposition — 'the Titan gods' (*θεοί* apposed to *Τιτῆνες*: the Titans-who-are-gods) and 'all who were born of Kronos' (the Olympians); rendered as apposition with Evelyn-White, not as a three-item list (resolving THEO-630). The framing point: both sides are *θεοί* — the Olympians too are *θεοί, δωτῆρες ἐάων* 'gods, givers of good things' (633, 664, the very hemistich of 46/111) — so the Titanomachy is a war of gods against gods (a theomachy), not gods against monsters. The transliteration 'Titans' is governed by `titanes-folk-etymology-theogony`; the both-sides-are-gods framing by `titanomachy-both-sides-gods-theomachy-theogony`. **Lens-discipline / comparative apparatus (clearly labeled):** the Titanomachy is the Greek instance of the wider Near-Eastern succession-conflict / theomachy pattern documented for the Ugaritic–Akkadian–Hebrew corpus in the central `chaoskampf-sea-conflict-cross-corpus` entry; per the signed-off Block-A/B non-fusion precedent that central entry is deliberately NOT extended to the Theogony, and the convergence — together with any Wheel-of-Heaven Theomachy-as-history reading — is confined to this apparatus, kept out of both the surface and the philological claim.

lines.text: ἀντίον ἀλλήλοισι διὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας,
lines.translit: antion allēloisi dia krateras hysminas

i18n.en: against one another in fierce battles:

lines.text: οἳ μὲν ἀφʼ ὑψηλῆς Ὄθρυος Τιτῆνες ἀγαυοί,
lines.translit: hoi men aph' hypsēlēs Othryos Titēnes agauoi

i18n.en: on the one side the glorious Titans from high Othrys,

lines.text: οἳ δʼ ἄρʼ ἀπʼ Οὐλύμποιο θεοί, δωτῆρες ἐάων,
lines.translit: hoi d' ar' ap' Oulympoio theoi dōtēres eaōn

i18n.en: and on the other the gods, givers of good things, from Olympos,

lines.text: οὓς τέκεν ἠύκομος Ῥείη Κρόνῳ εὐνηθεῖσα.
lines.translit: hous teken ēukomos Rheiē Kronō eunētheisa

i18n.en: whom fair-haired Rhea bore, having lain with Kronos.

lines.text: οἵ ῥα τότʼ ἀλλήλοισι χόλον θυμαλγέʼ ἔχοντες
lines.translit: hoi rha tot' allēloisi cholon thymalge' echontes

i18n.en: These then, holding heart-grieving anger against one another,

lines.text: συνεχέως ἐμάχοντο δέκα πλείους ἐνιαυτούς·
lines.translit: synecheōs emachonto deka pleious eniautous

i18n.en: fought continuously for ten full years and more;

lines.text: οὐδέ τις ἦν ἔριδος χαλεπῆς λύσις οὐδὲ τελευτὴ
lines.translit: oude tis ēn eridos chalepēs lysis oude teleutē

i18n.en: and there was no release from the grievous strife, nor any end,

lines.text: οὐδετέροις, ἶσον δὲ τέλος τέτατο πτολέμοιο.
lines.translit: oudeterois ison de telos tetato ptolemoio

i18n.en: for either side, but the issue of the war hung evenly balanced.

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ὅτε δὴ κείνοισι παρέσχεθεν ἄρμενα πάντα,
lines.translit: all' hote dē keinoisi pareschethen armena panta

i18n.en: But when he had provided those with all things fitting,

lines.text: νέκταρ τʼ ἀμβροσίην τε, τά περ θεοὶ αὐτοὶ ἔδουσι,
lines.translit: nektar t' ambrosiēn te ta per theoi autoi edousi
