i18n.en: nectar and ambrosia, which the gods themselves eat,

lines.text: πάντων ἐν στήθεσσιν ἀέξετο θυμὸς ἀγήνωρ.
lines.translit: pantōn en stēthessin aexeto thymos agēnōr

i18n.en: the proud spirit grew in the breasts of all;

lines.text: ὡς νέκταρ τʼ ἐπάσαντο καὶ ἀμβροσίην ἐρατεινήν,
lines.translit: hōs nektar t' epasanto kai ambrosiēn erateinēn

i18n.en: and when they had tasted the nectar and the lovely ambrosia,

lines.text: δὴ τότε τοῖς μετέειπε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε·
lines.translit: dē tote tois meteeipe patēr andrōn te theōn te

i18n.en: then the father of men and gods spoke among them:

lines.text: κέκλυτε μευ, Γαίης τε καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀγλαὰ τέκνα,
lines.translit: keklyte meu Gaiēs te kai Ouranou aglaa tekna

i18n.en: “Hear me, glorious children of Gaia and Ouranos,

lines.text: ὄφρʼ εἴπω, τά με θυμὸς ἐνὶ στήθεσσι κελεύει.
lines.translit: ophr' eipō ta me thymos eni stēthessi keleuei

i18n.en: that I may say what the heart within my breast bids me.

lines.text: ἤδη γὰρ μάλα δηρὸν ἐναντίοι ἀλλήλοισι
lines.translit: ēdē gar mala dēron enantioi allēloisi

i18n.en: For now a very long time, opposed to one another,

lines.text: νίκης καὶ κράτεος πέρι μαρνάμεθʼ ἤματα πάντα
lines.translit: nikēs kai krateos peri marnameth' ēmata panta

i18n.en: we have fought every day for victory and power,

notes.official: *νίκης καὶ κράτεος πέρι μαρνάμεθʼ* 'we have fought for victory and power' (647): in the Titanomachy *νίκη* 'victory' — and likewise *βίη* 'might/force' elsewhere in the battle — are common nouns, kept distinct from the personified Styx-children *Nike* and *Bia* (384–385, Block B) governed by the personified-abstractions entry; this ratifies the Translator's common-noun rendering. *κράτος* 'power' is tracked by `kratos-phertatos-sovereignty-vocabulary-theogony` (also 662).

lines.text: Τιτῆνές τε θεοὶ καὶ ὅσοι Κρόνου ἐκγενόμεσθα.
lines.translit: Titēnes te theoi kai hosoi Kronou ekgenomestha

i18n.en: the Titan gods, and we who were born of Kronos.

lines.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ μεγάλην τε βίην καὶ χεῖρας ἀάπτους
lines.translit: hymeis de megalēn te biēn kai cheiras aaptous

i18n.en: But do you show great might and irresistible hands

lines.text: φαίνετε Τιτήνεσσιν ἐναντίοι ἐν δαῒ λυγρῇ
lines.translit: phainete Titēnessin enantioi en dai lygrē

i18n.en: against the Titans in the baleful conflict,

lines.text: μνησάμενοι φιλότητος ἐνηέος, ὅσσα παθόντες
lines.translit: mnēsamenoi philotētos enēeos hossa pathontes

i18n.en: remembering our kindly friendship, and how, after all you suffered,

lines.text: ἐς φάος ἂψ ἀφίκεσθε δυσηλεγέος ὑπὸ δεσμοῦ
lines.translit: es phaos aps aphikesthe dysēlegeos hypo desmou

i18n.en: you came back again to the light out of your cruel bondage,

lines.text: ἡμετέρας διὰ βουλὰς ὑπὸ ζόφου ἠερόεντος.
lines.translit: hēmeteras dia boulas hypo zophou ēeroentos

i18n.en: through our counsels, out of the misty gloom.”

lines.text: ὣς φάτο· τὸν δʼ ἐξαῦτις ἀμείβετο Κόττος ἀμύμων·
lines.translit: hōs phato ton d' exautis ameibeto Kottos amymōn

i18n.en: So he spoke; and blameless Kottos answered him again:

lines.text: Δαιμόνιʼ, οὐκ ἀδάητα πιφαύσκεαι· ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτοὶ
lines.translit: Daimoni' ouk adaēta piphauskeai alla kai autoi

i18n.en: “Divine one, you tell us nothing we do not know; but we too

lines.text: ἴδμεν, ὅ τοι περὶ μὲν πραπίδες, περὶ δʼ ἐστὶ νόημα,
lines.translit: idmen ho toi peri men prapides peri d' esti noēma

i18n.en: know that your wits surpass all, and your understanding surpasses all,

lines.text: ἀλκτὴρ δʼ ἀθανάτοισιν ἀρῆς γένεο κρυεροῖο.
lines.translit: alktēr d' athanatoisin arēs geneo kryeroio

i18n.en: and that you became a defender of the immortals from chilling ruin;

lines.text: σῇσι δʼ ἐπιφροσύνῃσιν ὑπὸ ζόφου ἠερόεντος
lines.translit: sēsi d' epiphrosynēsin hypo zophou ēeroentos

i18n.en: and by your prudent counsel, out of the misty gloom,

lines.text: ἄψορρον δʼ† ἐξαῦτις ἀμειλίκτων ὑπὸ δεσμῶν
lines.translit: apsorron d' exautis ameiliktōn hypo desmōn

i18n.en: back once more from under the pitiless bonds,

notes.official: Source quirk preserved verbatim: the edition prints an obelus (†) after *δʼ* at 659 (*ἄψορρον δʼ† ἐξαῦτις ἀμειλίκτων ὑπὸ δεσμῶν*), marking a transmitted-text crux / suspected corruption. The daggered text is kept as-is in the source field and rendered per the received sense ('back once more from under the pitiless bonds'); it is not silently emended.

lines.text: ἠλύθομεν, Κρόνου υἱὲ ἄναξ, ἀνάελπτα παθόντες.
lines.translit: ēlythomen Kronou hyie anax anaelpta pathontes

i18n.en: we have come, O lord, son of Kronos, having suffered things beyond hope.

lines.text: τῷ καὶ νῦν ἀτενεῖ τε νόῳ καὶ ἐπίφρονι βουλῇ
lines.translit: tō kai nyn atenei te noō kai epiphroni boulē

i18n.en: And so now with steadfast mind and prudent counsel

lines.text: ῥυσόμεθα κράτος ὑμὸν ἐν αἰνῇ δηϊοτῆτι
lines.translit: rhysometha kratos hymon en ainē dēiotēti

i18n.en: we shall defend your power in the dread conflict,

lines.text: μαρνάμενοι Τιτῆσιν ἀνὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας.
lines.translit: marnamenoi Titēsin ana krateras hysminas

i18n.en: fighting with the Titans through the fierce battles.”

lines.text: ὣς φάτʼ· ἐπῄνεσσαν δὲ θεοί, δωτῆρες ἐάων,
lines.translit: hōs phat' epēnessan de theoi dōtēres eaōn

i18n.en: So he spoke; and the gods, givers of good things, praised him,

lines.text: μῦθον ἀκούσαντες· πολέμου δʼ ἐλιλαίετο θυμὸς
lines.translit: mython akousantes polemou d' elilaieto thymos

i18n.en: when they heard his word; and their spirit longed for war

lines.text: μᾶλλον ἔτʼ ἢ τὸ πάροιθε· μάχην δʼ ἀμέγαρτον ἔγειραν
lines.translit: mallon et' ē to paroithe machēn d' amegarton egeiran

i18n.en: even more than before; and they roused up dismal battle,

lines.text: πάντες, θήλειαι τε καὶ ἄρσενες, ἤματι κείνῳ,
lines.translit: pantes thēleiai te kai arsenes ēmati keinō

i18n.en: all of them, female and male alike, on that day,

lines.text: Τιτῆνές τε θεοὶ καὶ ὅσοι Κρόνου ἐξεγένοντο,
lines.translit: Titēnes te theoi kai hosoi Kronou exegenonto

i18n.en: the Titan gods, and all who were born of Kronos,

lines.text: οὕς τε Ζεὺς Ἐρέβευσφιν ὑπὸ χθονὸς ἧκε φόωσδε
lines.translit: hous te Zeus Erebeusphin hypo chthonos hēke phoōsde

i18n.en: and those whom Zeus sent up to the light from Erebos beneath the earth,

lines.text: δεινοί τε κρατεροί τε, βίην ὑπέροπλον ἔχοντες.
lines.translit: deinoi te krateroi te biēn hyperoplon echontes

i18n.en: terrible and strong, having overweening might.

lines.text: τῶν ἑκατὸν μὲν χεῖρες ἀπʼ ὤμων ἀίσσοντο
lines.translit: tōn hekaton men cheires ap' ōmōn aissonto

i18n.en: From their shoulders sprang a hundred arms,

lines.text: πᾶσιν ὁμῶς, κεφαλαὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ πεντήκοντα
lines.translit: pasin homōs kephalai de hekastō pentēkonta

i18n.en: for each alike, and fifty heads for each

lines.text: ἐξ ὤμων ἐπέφυκον ἐπὶ στιβαροῖσι μέλεσσιν.
lines.translit: ex ōmōn epephykon epi stibaroisi melessin

i18n.en: grew from the shoulders upon their sturdy limbs.

lines.text: οἳ τότε Τιτήνεσσι κατέσταθεν ἐν δαῒ λυγρῇ
lines.translit: hoi tote Titēnessi katestathen en dai lygrē

i18n.en: These then stood against the Titans in the baleful conflict,

lines.text: πέτρας ἠλιβάτους στιβαρῇς ἐν χερσὶν ἔχοντες.
lines.translit: petras ēlibatous stibarēs en chersin echontes

i18n.en: holding huge rocks in their sturdy hands.

lines.text: Τιτῆνες δʼ ἑτέρωθεν ἐκαρτύναντο φάλαγγας
lines.translit: Titēnes d' heterōthen ekartynanto phalangas

i18n.en: And the Titans on the other side strengthened their ranks

lines.text: προφρονέως, χειρῶν τε βίης θʼ ἅμα ἔργον ἔφαινον
lines.translit: prophroneōs cheirōn te biēs th' hama ergon ephainon

i18n.en: eagerly, and both sides showed the work of hands and of might;

lines.text: ἀμφότεροι· δεινὸν δὲ περίαχε πόντος ἀπείρων,
lines.translit: amphoteroi deinon de periache pontos apeirōn

i18n.en: and terribly the boundless sea resounded round about,

lines.text: γῆ δὲ μέγʼ ἐσμαράγησεν, ἐπέστενε δʼ οὐρανὸς εὐρὺς
lines.translit: gē de meg' esmaragēsen epestene d' ouranos eurys

i18n.en: and the earth crashed loudly, and the wide heaven groaned

lines.text: σειόμενος, πεδόθεν δὲ τινάσσετο μακρὸς Ὄλυμπος
lines.translit: seiomenos pedothen de tinasseto makros Olympos

i18n.en: as it was shaken; and tall Olympos trembled from its base

lines.text: ῥιπῇ ὕπʼ ἀθανάτων, ἔνοσις δʼ ἵκανε βαρεῖα
lines.translit: rhipē hyp' athanatōn enosis d' hikane bareia

i18n.en: under the onset of the immortals; and a heavy quaking reached

lines.text: Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα, ποδῶν τʼ αἰπεῖα ἰωὴ
lines.translit: Tartaron ēeroenta podōn t' aipeia iōē

i18n.en: misty Tartaros, and the shrill din of countless feet

notes.official: First Block-C occurrence of *Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα* 'misty Tartaros'; the quaking of the Titanomachy reaches down to it. See on 721; governed by `tartaros-underworld-vocabulary-theogony`.

lines.text: ἀσπέτου ἰωχμοῖο βολάων τε κρατεράων·
lines.translit: aspetou iōchmoio bolaōn te krateraōn

i18n.en: and of the mighty missiles in their unspeakable pursuit;

lines.text: ὣς ἄρʼ ἐπʼ ἀλλήλοις ἵεσαν βέλεα στονόεντα.
lines.translit: hōs ar' ep' allēlois hiesan belea stonoenta

i18n.en: so did they hurl their groan-causing shafts at one another.

lines.text: φωνὴ δʼ ἀμφοτέρων ἵκετʼ οὐρανὸν ἀστερόεντα
lines.translit: phōnē d' amphoterōn hiket' ouranon asteroenta

i18n.en: And the shout of both reached the starry heaven,

lines.text: κεκλομένων· οἳ δὲ ξύνισαν μεγάλῳ ἀλαλητῷ.
lines.translit: keklomenōn hoi de xynisan megalō alalētō

i18n.en: as they called out; and they closed with a great war-cry.

lines.text: οὐδʼ ἄρʼ ἔτι Ζεὺς ἴσχεν ἑὸν μένος, ἀλλά νυ τοῦ γε
lines.translit: oud' ar' eti Zeus ischen heon menos alla ny tou ge

i18n.en: And now Zeus no longer held back his strength, but then

lines.text: εἶθαρ μὲν μένεος πλῆντο φρένες, ἐκ δέ τε πᾶσαν
lines.translit: eithar men meneos plēnto phrenes ek de te pasan

i18n.en: at once his heart was filled with fury, and he showed forth

lines.text: φαῖνε βίην· ἄμυδις δʼ ἄρʼ ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἠδʼ ἀπʼ Ὀλύμπου
lines.translit: phaine biēn amydis d' ar' ap' ouranou ēd' ap' Olympou

i18n.en: all his might; and from heaven and from Olympos together

lines.text: ἀστράπτων ἔστειχε συνωχαδόν· οἱ δὲ κεραυνοὶ
lines.translit: astraptōn esteiche synōchadon hoi de keraunoi

i18n.en: he came, hurling lightning without ceasing; and the thunderbolts

lines.text: ἴκταρ ἅμα βροντῇ τε καὶ ἀστεροπῇ ποτέοντο
lines.translit: iktar hama brontē te kai asteropē poteonto

i18n.en: flew thick together, with thunder and with lightning,

lines.text: χειρὸς ἄπο στιβαρῆς, ἱερὴν φλόγα εἰλυφόωντες
lines.translit: cheiros apo stibarēs hierēn phloga eilyphoōntes

i18n.en: from his sturdy hand, whirling a holy flame,

lines.text: ταρφέες· ἀμφὶ δὲ γαῖα φερέσβιος ἐσμαράγιζε
lines.translit: tarphees amphi de gaia pheresbios esmaragize

i18n.en: close-packed; and round about the life-giving earth crashed

lines.text: καιομένη, λάκε δʼ ἀμφὶ πυρὶ μεγάλʼ ἄσπετος ὕλη.
lines.translit: kaiomenē lake d' amphi pyri megal' aspetos hylē

i18n.en: as it burned, and the vast forest crackled loudly with fire.

lines.text: ἔζεε δὲ χθὼν πᾶσα καὶ Ὠκεανοῖο ῥέεθρα
lines.translit: ezee de chthōn pasa kai Ōkeanoio rheethra

i18n.en: All the earth boiled, and the streams of Okeanos,

lines.text: πόντος τʼ ἀτρύγετος· τοὺς δʼ ἄμφεπε θερμὸς ἀυτμὴ
lines.translit: pontos t' atrygetos tous d' amphepe thermos autmē

i18n.en: and the barren sea; and the hot blast enveloped

lines.text: Τιτῆνας χθονίους, φλὸξ δʼ αἰθέρα δῖαν ἵκανεν
lines.translit: Titēnas chthonious phlox d' aithera dian hikanen

i18n.en: the earth-born Titans, and the flame reached the divine upper air,

lines.text: ἄσπετος, ὄσσε δʼ ἄμερδε καὶ ἰφθίμων περ ἐόντων
lines.translit: aspetos osse d' amerde kai iphthimōn per eontōn

i18n.en: unspeakable, and it blinded the eyes even of the strong,

lines.text: αὐγὴ μαρμαίρουσα κεραυνοῦ τε στεροπῆς τε.
lines.translit: augē marmairousa keraunou te steropēs te

i18n.en: the flashing gleam of the thunderbolt and lightning.

lines.text: καῦμα δὲ θεσπέσιον κάτεχεν Χάος· εἴσατο δʼ ἄντα
lines.translit: kauma de thespesion katechen Chaos eisato d' anta

i18n.en: A marvellous heat seized Chaos; and it seemed, to look upon,

notes.official: *καῦμα δὲ θεσπέσιον κάτεχεν Χάος* 'a marvellous heat seized Chaos' (700): *Χάος* here is the primordial gap/void of 116 (the `chaos-primordial-chasm-void-theogony` sense), now filled with the heat of Zeus's thunderbolts — the cosmogonic 'yawning gap' reappearing at the cosmic climax of the war, not the later 'disorder'. Rendered 'Chaos' with Evelyn-White.

lines.text: ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ἰδεῖν ἠδʼ οὔασι ὄσσαν ἀκοῦσαι
lines.translit: ophthalmoisin idein ēd' ouasi ossan akousai

i18n.en: with the eyes, and to hear the sound with the ears,

lines.text: αὔτως, ὡς εἰ Γαῖα καὶ Οὐρανὸς εὐρὺς ὕπερθε
lines.translit: autōs hōs ei Gaia kai Ouranos eurys hyperthe

i18n.en: just as if earth and wide heaven above

lines.text: πίλνατο· τοῖος γάρ κε μέγας ὑπὸ δοῦπος ὀρώρει
lines.translit: pilnato toios gar ke megas hypo doupos orōrei

i18n.en: were coming together; for such a great crash would arise,

lines.text: τῆς μὲν ἐρειπομένης, τοῦ δʼ ὑψόθεν ἐξεριπόντος·
lines.translit: tēs men ereipomenēs tou d' hypsothen exeripontos

i18n.en: as she was shattered and he came crashing down from on high;

lines.text: τόσσος δοῦπος ἔγεντο θεῶν ἔριδι ξυνιόντων.
lines.translit: tossos doupos egento theōn eridi xyniontōn

i18n.en: so great a crash arose as the gods clashed in strife.

lines.text: σὺν δʼ ἄνεμοι ἔνοσίν τε κονίην τʼ ἐσφαράγιζον
lines.translit: syn d' anemoi enosin te koniēn t' espharagizon

i18n.en: And the winds together stirred up quaking and dust,

lines.text: βροντήν τε στεροπήν τε καὶ αἰθαλόεντα κεραυνόν,
lines.translit: brontēn te steropēn te kai aithaloenta keraunon

i18n.en: thunder and lightning and the blazing thunderbolt,

lines.text: κῆλα Διὸς μεγάλοιο, φέρον δʼ ἰαχήν τʼ ἐνοπήν τε
lines.translit: kēla Dios megaloio pheron d' iachēn t' enopēn te

i18n.en: the shafts of great Zeus, and they carried the shout and the cry

lines.text: ἐς μέσον ἀμφοτέρων· ὄτοβος δʼ ἄπλητος ὀρώρει
lines.translit: es meson amphoterōn otobos d' aplētos orōrei

i18n.en: into the midst of both sides; and an awful din arose

lines.text: σμερδαλέης ἔριδος, κάρτος δʼ ἀνεφαίνετο ἔργων.
lines.translit: smerdaleēs eridos kartos d' anephaineto ergōn

i18n.en: of dread strife, and the might of their deeds was shown forth.

lines.text: ἐκλίνθη δὲ μάχη· πρὶν δʼ ἀλλήλοις ἐπέχοντες
lines.translit: eklinthē de machē prin d' allēlois epechontes

i18n.en: And the battle turned; before, holding out against one another,

lines.text: ἐμμενέως ἐμάχοντο διὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας.
lines.translit: emmeneōs emachonto dia krateras hysminas

i18n.en: they had fought steadily through the fierce battles.

lines.text: οἳ δʼ ἄρʼ ἐνὶ πρώτοισι μάχην δριμεῖαν ἔγειραν
lines.translit: hoi d' ar' eni prōtoisi machēn drimeian egeiran

i18n.en: But now among the foremost they roused up bitter battle,

lines.text: Κόττος τε Βριάρεώς τε Γύης τʼ ἄατος πολέμοιο,
lines.translit: Kottos te Briareōs te Gyēs t' aatos polemoio

i18n.en: Kottos and Briareos and Gyes, insatiate of war,

lines.text: οἵ ῥα τριηκοσίας πέτρας στιβαρῶν ἀπὸ χειρῶν
lines.translit: hoi rha triēkosias petras stibarōn apo cheirōn

i18n.en: who hurled three hundred rocks from their sturdy hands

lines.text: πέμπον ἐπασσυτέρας, κατὰ δʼ ἐσκίασαν βελέεσσι
lines.translit: pempon epassyteras kata d' eskiasan beleessi

i18n.en: one upon another, and overshadowed with their missiles

lines.text: Τιτῆνας, καὶ τοὺς μὲν ὑπὸ χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης
lines.translit: Titēnas kai tous men hypo chthonos euryodeiēs

i18n.en: the Titans; and they sent them beneath the wide-wayed earth,

lines.text: πέμψαν καὶ δεσμοῖσιν ἐν ἀργαλέοισιν ἔδησαν
lines.translit: pempsan kai desmoisin en argaleoisin edēsan

i18n.en: and bound them in grievous bonds,

lines.text: χερσὶν νικήσαντες ὑπερθύμους περ ἐόντας,
lines.translit: chersin nikēsantes hyperthymous per eontas

i18n.en: having conquered them with their hands, for all their high spirit,

lines.text: τόσσον ἔνερθʼ ὑπὸ γῆς, ὅσον οὐρανός ἐστʼ ἀπὸ γαίης·
lines.translit: tosson enerth' hypo gēs hoson ouranos est' apo gaiēs

i18n.en: as far beneath the earth as heaven is from the earth;

lines.text: τόσσον γάρ τʼ ἀπὸ γῆς ἐς Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα.
lines.translit: tosson gar t' apo gēs es Tartaron ēeroenta

i18n.en: for so far is it from the earth down to misty Tartaros.

notes.official: Tartaros. The defeated Titans are hurled 'as far beneath the earth as heaven is from the earth' (720) into *Τάρταρον ἠερόεντα* 'misty Tartaros' (682, 721, 725), fenced with bronze (726) behind bronze doors (732–733) and guarded by the Hundred-Handers (734–735). *Τάρταρος* is transliterated (standard); the vocabulary follows Evelyn-White. See `tartaros-underworld-vocabulary-theogony`. **Reception apparatus (labeled):** the derived Greek verb *ταρταρόω* 'to cast down to Tartaros' is used at 2 Peter 2:4 of the imprisoned rebel angels — a datum of the word's later Greco-Jewish/Christian reception, recorded as apparatus only; there is no central Tartaros entry and none is created or extended (non-fusion precedent).

lines.text: ἐννέα γὰρ νύκτας τε καὶ ἤματα χάλκεος ἄκμων
lines.translit: ennea gar nyktas te kai ēmata chalkeos akmōn

i18n.en: For nine nights and days would a bronze anvil,

lines.text: οὐρανόθεν κατιὼν δεκάτῃ κʼ ἐς γαῖαν ἵκοιτο·
lines.translit: ouranothen katiōn dekatē k' es gaian hikoito

i18n.en: falling from heaven, on the tenth reach the earth;

lines.text: ἐννέα δʼ αὖ νύκτας τε καὶ ἤματα χάλκεος ἄκμων
lines.translit: ennea d' au nyktas te kai ēmata chalkeos akmōn

i18n.en: and again for nine nights and days would a bronze anvil,

lines.text: ἐκ γαίης κατιὼν δεκάτῃ κʼ ἐς Τάρταρον ἵκοι.
lines.translit: ek gaiēs katiōn dekatē k' es Tartaron hikoi

i18n.en: falling from the earth, on the tenth reach Tartaros.

lines.text: τὸν πέρι χάλκεον ἕρκος ἐλήλαται· ἀμφὶ δέ μιν νὺξ
lines.translit: ton peri chalkeon herkos elēlatai amphi de min nyx

i18n.en: Round it a bronze fence is driven; and about it night

lines.text: τριστοιχεὶ κέχυται περὶ δειρήν· αὐτὰρ ὕπερθεν
lines.translit: tristoichei kechytai peri deirēn autar hyperthen

i18n.en: is poured in three rows about its throat; and above

lines.text: γῆς ῥίζαι πεφύασι καὶ ἀτρυγέτοιο θαλάσσης.
lines.translit: gēs rhizai pephyasi kai atrygetoio thalassēs

i18n.en: grow the roots of the earth and of the barren sea.

lines.text: ἔνθα θεοὶ Τιτῆνες ὑπὸ ζόφῳ ἠερόεντι
lines.translit: entha theoi Titēnes hypo zophō ēeroenti

i18n.en: There the Titan gods are hidden beneath the misty gloom,

lines.text: κεκρύφαται βουλῇσι Διὸς νεφεληγερέταο
lines.translit: kekryphatai boulēsi Dios nephelēgeretao

i18n.en: by the counsels of Zeus the cloud-gatherer,

lines.text: χώρῳ ἐν εὐρώεντι, πελώρης ἔσχατα γαίης.
lines.translit: chōrō en eurōenti pelōrēs eschata gaiēs

i18n.en: in a dank place, at the ends of the huge earth.

lines.text: τοῖς οὐκ ἐξιτόν ἐστι. θύρας δʼ ἐπέθηκε Ποσειδέων
lines.translit: tois ouk exiton esti thyras d' epethēke Poseideōn

i18n.en: For them there is no way out. Poseidon set doors of bronze upon it,

lines.text: χαλκείας, τεῖχος δὲ περοίχεται ἀμφοτέρωθεν.
lines.translit: chalkeias teichos de peroichetai amphoterōthen

i18n.en: and a wall runs round it on both sides.

lines.text: ἔνθα Γύης Κόττος τε καὶ Ὀβριάρεως μεγάθυμος
lines.translit: entha Gyēs Kottos te kai Obriareōs megathymos

i18n.en: There dwell Gyes, Kottos, and great-hearted Briareos,

notes.official: *Ὀβριάρεως* (734) is the metrical/dialectal doublet of *Βριάρεως* (617, 714); it is normalized to 'Briareos' in the surface for consistency across the name's four occurrences (149, 617, 714, 734), the source form *Ὀβριάρεως* kept verbatim in the text field. The prothetic-omicron *Ὀβρ-* form is a Hesiodic metrical variant (West 1966, ad 734); at *Iliad* 1.403 the name appears as *Βριάρεως* in the separate gods-vs-men name-doublet with *Αἰγαίων* — a different phenomenon from the spelling variation here. Surface change vs the draft ('Obriareos' → 'Briareos'); governed by `dialectal-theonym-normalization-theogony`.

lines.text: ναίουσιν, φύλακες πιστοὶ Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο.
lines.translit: naiousin phylakes pistoi Dios aigiochoio

i18n.en: the faithful guardians of aegis-holding Zeus.

lines.text: ἔνθα δὲ γῆς δνοφερῆς καὶ Ταρτάρου ἠερόεντος
lines.translit: entha de gēs dnopherēs kai Tartarou ēeroentos

i18n.en: There, of the murky earth and of misty Tartaros,

notes.official: *Ταρτάρου ἠερόεντος* 'misty Tartaros' (736) opens the cosmography of the world's *πηγαί* and *πείρατα* 'sources and limits' (736–745), continuing the Tartaros description begun at 720–735 (Block C). Transliterated 'Tartaros' with the descriptive vocabulary following Evelyn-White; `tartaros-underworld-vocabulary-theogony`, whose scope is extended to the Block-D prison/cosmography sites (736, 807, 841, 851, 868). *γῆς … οὐρανοῦ* remain common nouns 'earth … heaven' per `ouranos-gaia-cosmogony-personification-boundary-theogony`.

lines.text: πόντου τʼ ἀτρυγέτοιο καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος
lines.translit: pontou t' atrygetoio kai ouranou asteroentos

i18n.en: and of the barren sea and of the starry heaven,

lines.text: ἑξείης πάντων πηγαὶ καὶ πείρατʼ ἔασιν
lines.translit: hexeiēs pantōn pēgai kai peirat' easin

i18n.en: are the sources and limits of all things, in order, one after another,

lines.text: ἀργαλέʼ εὐρώεντα, τά τε στυγέουσι θεοί περ,
lines.translit: argale' eurōenta ta te stygeousi theoi per

i18n.en: grievous and dank, which even the gods abhor,

lines.text: χάσμα μέγʼ, οὐδέ κε πάντα τελεσφόρον εἰς ἐνιαυτὸν
lines.translit: chasma meg' oude ke panta telesphoron eis eniauton

i18n.en: a great chasm; and not even in a whole completed year

notes.official: *χάσμα μέγʼ* 'a great chasm' (740): the gulf below the bronze threshold of Tartaros is a *χάσμα*, from the same root *χα-* (*χαίνω/χάσκω* 'to gape, yawn') as *Χάος* at 116 — the primordial 'yawning gap' reappearing as the abyss beneath the world. Rendered 'a great chasm' with Evelyn-White; the *χάσμα ~ Χάος* cognation is philological, not an identity of referents (`chaos-primordial-chasm-void-theogony`, extended to 740, 814; cf. the note on 700, where Chaos itself recurs at the climax of the Titanomachy).

lines.text: οὖδας ἵκοιτʼ, εἰ πρῶτα πυλέων ἔντοσθε γένοιτο,
lines.translit: oudas hikoit' ei prōta pyleōn entosthe genoito

i18n.en: would one reach the floor, if first he passed within the gates,

lines.text: ἀλλά κεν ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα φέροι πρὸ θύελλα θυέλλῃ
lines.translit: alla ken entha kai entha pheroi pro thyella thyellē

i18n.en: but storm upon storm would carry him this way and that,

lines.text: ἀργαλέη· δεινὸν δὲ καὶ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι
lines.translit: argaleē deinon de kai athanatoisi theoisi

i18n.en: a grievous thing; and dread even to the immortal gods

lines.text: τοῦτο τέρας. Νυκτὸς δʼ ἐρεβεννῆς οἰκία δεινὰ
lines.translit: touto teras Nyktos d' erebennēs oikia deina

i18n.en: is this portent. And the terrible houses of dark Night

lines.text: ἕστηκεν νεφέλῃς κεκαλυμμένα κυανέῃσιν.
lines.translit: hestēken nephelēs kekalymmena kyaneēsin

i18n.en: stand shrouded in dark clouds.

lines.text: τῶν πρόσθʼ Ἰαπετοῖο πάις ἔχει οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν
lines.translit: tōn prosth' Iapetoio pais echei ouranon euryn

i18n.en: In front of these the son of Iapetos holds the wide heaven,

lines.text: ἑστηὼς κεφαλῇ τε καὶ ἀκαμάτῃσι χέρεσσιν
lines.translit: hestēōs kephalē te kai akamatēsi cheressin

i18n.en: standing, with his head and unwearying hands,

lines.text: ἀστεμφέως, ὅθι Νύξ τε καὶ Ἡμέρη ἆσσον ἰοῦσαι
lines.translit: astempheōs hothi Nyx te kai Hēmerē asson iousai

i18n.en: unmoving, where Night and Day draw near

lines.text: ἀλλήλας προσέειπον, ἀμειβόμεναι μέγαν οὐδὸν
lines.translit: allēlas proseeipon ameibomenai megan oudon

i18n.en: and greet each other as they pass the great threshold

lines.text: χάλκεον· ἣ μὲν ἔσω καταβήσεται, ἣ δὲ θύραζε
lines.translit: chalkeon hē men esō katabēsetai hē de thyraze

i18n.en: of bronze; the one will go down within, while the other

lines.text: ἔρχεται, οὐδέ ποτʼ ἀμφοτέρας δόμος ἐντὸς ἐέργει,
lines.translit: erchetai oude pot' amphoteras domos entos eergei

i18n.en: goes forth, and never does the house hold both within,

lines.text: ἀλλʼ αἰεὶ ἑτέρη γε δόμων ἔκτοσθεν ἐοῦσα
lines.translit: all' aiei heterē ge domōn ektosthen eousa

i18n.en: but always one, being outside the house,

lines.text: γαῖαν ἐπιστρέφεται, ἣ δʼ αὖ δόμου ἐντὸς ἐοῦσα
lines.translit: gaian epistrephetai hē d' au domou entos eousa

i18n.en: ranges over the earth, while the other, being within the house,

lines.text: μίμνει τὴν αὐτῆς ὥρην ὁδοῦ, ἔστʼ ἂν ἵκηται,
lines.translit: mimnei tēn autēs hōrēn hodou est' an hikētai

i18n.en: awaits her own hour of journeying, until it comes;

lines.text: ἣ μὲν ἐπιχθονίοισι φάος πολυδερκὲς ἔχουσα,
lines.translit: hē men epichthonioisi phaos polyderkes echousa

i18n.en: the one holding a light of wide vision for those upon the earth,

lines.text: ἣ δʼ Ὕπνον μετὰ χερσί, κασίγνητον Θανάτοιο.
lines.translit: hē d' Hypnon meta chersi kasignēton Thanatoio

i18n.en: the other holding Sleep in her arms, the brother of Death—

lines.text: Νὺξ ὀλοή, νεφέλῃ κεκαλυμμένη ἠεροειδεῖ.
lines.translit: Nyx oloē nephelē kekalymmenē ēeroeidei

i18n.en: deadly Night, shrouded in cloudy mist.

lines.text: ἔνθα δὲ Νυκτὸς παῖδες ἐρεμνῆς οἰκίʼ ἔχουσιν,
lines.translit: entha de Nyktos paides eremnēs oiki' echousin

i18n.en: There the children of dark Night have their dwellings,

lines.text: Ὕπνος καὶ Θάνατος, δεινοὶ θεοί· οὐδέ ποτʼ αὐτοὺς
lines.translit: Hypnos kai Thanatos deinoi theoi oude pot' autous

i18n.en: Sleep and Death, dread gods; never does

lines.text: Ἠέλιος φαέθων ἐπιδέρκεται ἀκτίνεσσιν
lines.translit: Ēelios phaethōn epiderketai aktinessin

i18n.en: the shining Sun look upon them with his beams,

lines.text: οὐρανὸν εἲς ἀνιὼν οὐδʼ οὐρανόθεν καταβαίνων.
lines.translit: ouranon eis aniōn oud' ouranothen katabainōn

i18n.en: as he goes up into heaven or comes down from heaven.

notes.official: The source prints a grave accent on the proclitic *εἲς* (*οὐρανὸν εἲς ἀνιών*, 761) — a printing quirk of the edition. The transmitted form is kept verbatim in the source text field and the standard *εἰς* 'into' is construed in the English, per the source-fidelity convention (`source-orthographic-quirks-verbatim-theogony`; cf. the unaccented *Χρυσαωρ* at 281).

lines.text: τῶν δʼ ἕτερος γαῖάν τε καὶ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης
lines.translit: tōn d' heteros gaian te kai eurea nōta thalassēs

i18n.en: Of these the one roams quietly over the earth and the wide back of the sea,

lines.text: ἥσυχος ἀνστρέφεται καὶ μείλιχος ἀνθρώποισι,
lines.translit: hēsychos anstrephetai kai meilichos anthrōpoisi

i18n.en: gently, and is kindly to men;

lines.text: τοῦ δὲ σιδηρέη μὲν κραδίη, χάλκεον δέ οἱ ἦτορ
lines.translit: tou de sidēreē men kradiē chalkeon de hoi ētor

i18n.en: but the other has a heart of iron, and a spirit of bronze,

lines.text: νηλεὲς ἐν στήθεσσιν· ἔχει δʼ ὃν πρῶτα λάβῃσιν
lines.translit: nēlees en stēthessin echei d' hon prōta labēsin

i18n.en: pitiless within his breast; and he holds fast whomever he first seizes

lines.text: ἀνθρώπων· ἐχθρὸς δὲ καὶ ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσιν.
lines.translit: anthrōpōn echthros de kai athanatoisi theoisin

i18n.en: of men; and he is hateful even to the immortal gods.

lines.text: ἔνθα θεοῦ χθονίου πρόσθεν δόμοι ἠχήεντες
lines.translit: entha theou chthoniou prosthen domoi ēchēentes

i18n.en: There, in front, stand the echoing halls of the god of the underworld,

lines.text: ἰφθίμου τʼ Ἀίδεω καὶ ἐπαινῆς Περσεφονείης
lines.translit: iphthimou t' Aideō kai epainēs Persephoneiēs

i18n.en: mighty Hades, and of dread Persephone,

notes.official: *Ἀίδεω* (768) is the epic (unaspirated) genitive of *Ἅιδης* 'Hades', normalized to the standard 'Hades' in the surface exactly as at 455 (Block C), the source spelling kept verbatim in the text field; 'Hades' is the standard *Greek* form, not the Latin 'Pluto/Dis'. Governed by `dialectal-theonym-normalization-theogony`, whose scope is extended to the Block-D Hades sites (768, 774, 850). Distinct from *Ἀιδωνεύς* 'Aidoneus' (913), a fuller alternative name kept unnormalized — see the note there.

lines.text: ἑστᾶσιν, δεινὸς δὲ κύων προπάροιθε φυλάσσει
lines.translit: hestasin deinos de kyōn proparoithe phylassei

i18n.en: and a fearful hound keeps guard before them,

lines.text: νηλειής, τέχνην δὲ κακὴν ἔχει· ἐς μὲν ἰόντας
lines.translit: nēleiēs technēn de kakēn echei es men iontas

i18n.en: pitiless, and he has an evil trick: on those who come in

lines.text: σαίνει ὁμῶς οὐρῇ τε καὶ οὔασιν ἀμφοτέροισιν,
lines.translit: sainei homōs ourē te kai ouasin amphoteroisin

i18n.en: he fawns alike with his tail and both his ears,

lines.text: ἐξελθεῖν δʼ οὐκ αὖτις ἐᾷ πάλιν, ἀλλὰ δοκεύων
lines.translit: exelthein d' ouk autis ea palin alla dokeuōn

i18n.en: but he does not let them go out again; but, watching,

lines.text: ἐσθίει, ὅν κε λάβῃσι πυλέων ἔκτοσθεν ἰόντα.
lines.translit: esthiei hon ke labēsi pyleōn ektosthen ionta

i18n.en: he devours whomever he catches going out beyond the gates.

lines.text: ἰφθίμου τʼ Ἀίδεω καὶ ἐπαινῆς Περσεφονείης.
lines.translit: iphthimou t' Aideō kai epainēs Persephoneiēs

i18n.en: of mighty Hades and of dread Persephone.

notes.official: Line 774 (*ἰφθίμου τʼ Ἀίδεω καὶ ἐπαινῆς Περσεφονείης*) is athetized in the Perseus/West edition: it repeats 768 verbatim and is judged an interpolation resuming the house-of-Hades description after the Kerberos digression (769–773). Per the athetized-lines convention the transmitted line is retained and translated unmarked in the surface, the athetesis recorded here; *Ἀίδεω*→'Hades' as at 768. See `athetized-lines-convention-theogony` and `dialectal-theonym-normalization-theogony`.

lines.text: ἔνθα δὲ ναιετάει στυγερὴ θεὸς ἀθανάτοισι,
lines.translit: entha de naietaei stygerē theos athanatoisi

i18n.en: There dwells a goddess loathed by the immortals,

lines.text: δεινὴ Στύξ, θυγάτηρ ἀψορρόου Ὠκεανοῖο
lines.translit: deinē Styx thygatēr apsorroou Ōkeanoio

i18n.en: dread Styx, daughter of back-flowing Okeanos,

lines.text: πρεσβυτάτη· νόσφιν δὲ θεῶν κλυτὰ δώματα ναίει
lines.translit: presbytatē nosphin de theōn klyta dōmata naiei

i18n.en: the eldest; and apart from the gods she dwells in glorious halls

lines.text: μακρῇσιν πέτρῃσι κατηρεφέʼ· ἀμφὶ δὲ πάντη
lines.translit: makrēsin petrēsi katērephe' amphi de pantē

i18n.en: roofed over with great rocks; and on every side

lines.text: κίοσιν ἀργυρέοισι πρὸς οὐρανὸν ἐστήρικται.
lines.translit: kiosin argyreoisi pros ouranon estēriktai

i18n.en: they are propped toward heaven with silver pillars.

lines.text: παῦρα δὲ Θαύμαντος θυγάτηρ πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις
lines.translit: paura de Thaumantos thygatēr podas ōkea Iris

i18n.en: Seldom does the daughter of Thaumas, swift-footed Iris,

lines.text: ἀγγελίην πωλεῖται ἐπʼ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης.
lines.translit: angeliēn pōleitai ep' eurea nōta thalassēs

i18n.en: come with a message over the wide back of the sea.

lines.text: ὁππότʼ ἔρις καὶ νεῖκος ἐν ἀθανάτοισιν ὄρηται
lines.translit: hoppot' eris kai neikos en athanatoisin orētai

i18n.en: Whenever strife and quarrel arise among the immortals,

lines.text: καί ῥʼ ὅστις ψεύδηται Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἐχόντων,
lines.translit: kai rh' hostis pseudētai Olympia dōmat' echontōn

i18n.en: and one of those who have their homes on Olympos speaks falsely,

lines.text: Ζεὺς δέ τε Ἶριν ἔπεμψε θεῶν μέγαν ὅρκον ἐνεῖκαι
lines.translit: Zeus de te Irin epempse theōn megan horkon eneikai

i18n.en: then Zeus sends Iris to fetch the great oath of the gods

notes.official: *θεῶν μέγαν ὅρκον* 'the great oath of the gods' (784) repeats verbatim the phrase of 400 (Block B) and opens the oath-procedure (775–806): Iris fetches the Styx-water in a golden jug (*προχόῳ*, 785), and a forsworn god lies breathless a full year (795–798) and is cut off from the gods for nine (801–804). Here *ὅρκος* is again the oath-*object* sworn by — the sanction-water, not the personified avenger *Horkos* (son of Eris, 231) nor the speech-act — restated at 805 (*τοῖον … ὅρκον ἔθεντο θεοί*). Rendered 'the great oath of the gods' with Evelyn-White; `horkos-styx-great-oath-theogony`, whose scope is extended from 400 to its payoff sites 784 and 805. **Lens-discipline note:** this is the poem's institution of a binding cosmic sanction, but the note stays at the philological level (the *horkos*-as-witness sense and the Styx/Horkos distinction); no covenant-cosmology reading is pressed into line or apparatus — cf. the non-extension of the central Hebrew *brit*/oath entries recorded in the Block-D report.

lines.text: τηλόθεν ἐν χρυσέῃ προχόῳ πολυώνυμον ὕδωρ
lines.translit: tēlothen en chryseē prochoō polyōnymon hydōr

i18n.en: from afar, in a golden jug, the far-famed water,

lines.text: ψυχρόν, ὅτʼ ἐκ πέτρης καταλείβεται ἠλιβάτοιο
lines.translit: psychron hot' ek petrēs kataleibetai ēlibatoio

i18n.en: the cold water that trickles down from a high, sheer rock;

lines.text: ὑψηλῆς· πολλὸν δὲ ὑπὸ χθονὸς εὐρυοδείης
lines.translit: hypsēlēs pollon de hypo chthonos euryodeiēs

i18n.en: and far beneath the wide-wayed earth,

lines.text: ἐξ ἱεροῦ ποταμοῖο ῥέει διὰ νύκτα μέλαιναν
lines.translit: ex hierou potamoio rheei dia nykta melainan

i18n.en: from a holy river it flows through the black night,

lines.text: Ὠκεανοῖο κέρας· δεκάτη δʼ ἐπὶ μοῖρα δέδασται·
lines.translit: Ōkeanoio keras dekatē d' epi moira dedastai

i18n.en: a branch of Okeanos; and a tenth part is allotted to her.

lines.text: ἐννέα μὲν περὶ γῆν τε καὶ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης
lines.translit: ennea men peri gēn te kai eurea nōta thalassēs

i18n.en: With nine streams, winding round the earth and the wide back of the sea

lines.text: δίνῃς ἀργυρέῃς εἱλιγμένος εἰς ἅλα πίπτει,
lines.translit: dinēs argyreēs heiligmenos eis hala piptei

i18n.en: in silver eddies, he falls into the salt sea;

lines.text: ἣ δὲ μίʼ ἐκ πέτρης προρέει μέγα πῆμα θεοῖσιν.
lines.translit: hē de mi' ek petrēs proreei mega pēma theoisin

i18n.en: but this one flows forth alone from a rock, a great bane to the gods.

lines.text: ὅς κεν τὴν ἐπίορκον ἀπολλείψας ἐπομόσσῃ
lines.translit: hos ken tēn epiorkon apolleipsas epomossē

i18n.en: Whoever of the immortals who hold the peak of snowy Olympos

lines.text: ἀθανάτων, οἳ ἔχουσι κάρη νιφόεντος Ὀλύμπου,
lines.translit: athanatōn hoi echousi karē niphoentos Olympou

i18n.en: pours a libation of it and swears falsely,

lines.text: κεῖται νήυτμος τετελεσμένον εἰς ἐνιαυτόν·
lines.translit: keitai nēytmos tetelesmenon eis eniauton

i18n.en: lies breathless for a full year;

lines.text: οὐδέ ποτʼ ἀμβροσίης καὶ νέκταρος ἔρχεται ἆσσον
lines.translit: oude pot' ambrosiēs kai nektaros erchetai asson

i18n.en: and never does he come near to ambrosia and nectar

lines.text: βρώσιος, ἀλλά τε κεῖται ἀνάπνευστος καὶ ἄναυδος
lines.translit: brōsios alla te keitai anapneustos kai anaudos

i18n.en: for food, but lies without breath and without voice

lines.text: στρωτοῖς ἐν λεχέεσσι, κακὸν δέ ἑ κῶμα καλύπτει.
lines.translit: strōtois en lecheessi kakon de he kōma kalyptei

i18n.en: on a spread couch, and an evil stupor covers him.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ νοῦσον τελέσῃ μέγαν εἰς ἐνιαυτόν,
lines.translit: autar epei nouson telesē megan eis eniauton

i18n.en: But when he has completed his sickness through the long year,

lines.text: ἄλλος γʼ ἐξ ἄλλου δέχεται χαλεπώτερος ἄεθλος.
lines.translit: allos g' ex allou dechetai chalepōteros aethlos

i18n.en: one harder trial follows another, one after the other.

lines.text: εἰνάετες δὲ θεῶν ἀπαμείρεται αἰὲν ἐόντων,
lines.translit: einaetes de theōn apameiretai aien eontōn

i18n.en: For nine years he is cut off from the gods who are forever,

lines.text: οὐδέ ποτʼ ἐς βουλὴν ἐπιμίσγεται οὐδʼ ἐπὶ δαῖτας
lines.translit: oude pot' es boulēn epimisgetai oud' epi daitas

i18n.en: and never does he join their council or their feasts

lines.text: ἐννέα πάντα ἔτεα· δεκάτῳ δʼ ἐπιμίσγεται αὖτις
lines.translit: ennea panta etea dekatō d' epimisgetai autis

i18n.en: for all nine years; but in the tenth he mingles again

lines.text: εἴρας ἐς ἀθανάτων, οἳ Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσιν.
lines.translit: eiras es athanatōn hoi Olympia dōmat' echousin

i18n.en: in the assemblies of the immortals who have their homes on Olympos.

lines.text: τοῖον ἄρʼ ὅρκον ἔθεντο θεοὶ Στυγὸς ἄφθιτον ὕδωρ
lines.translit: toion ar' horkon ethento theoi Stygos aphthiton hydōr

i18n.en: Such an oath did the gods make of the imperishable, primeval water

notes.official: *τοῖον ἄρʼ ὅρκον ἔθεντο θεοὶ Στυγὸς ἄφθιτον ὕδωρ / ὠγύγιον* 'such an oath the gods made of the imperishable, primeval water of Styx' (805–806): the closing frame of the oath-procedure, *ὅρκος* again the oath-object (the Styx-water) rather than the deity. Rendered with Evelyn-White; the second payoff site of `horkos-styx-great-oath-theogony` (see on 784).

lines.text: ὠγύγιον, τὸ δʼ ἵησι καταστυφέλου διὰ χώρου.
lines.translit: ōgygion to d' hiēsi katastyphelou dia chōrou

i18n.en: of Styx, which runs down through a rugged region.

lines.text: ἔνθα δὲ γῆς δνοφερῆς καὶ Ταρτάρου ἠερόεντος
lines.translit: entha de gēs dnopherēs kai Tartarou ēeroentos

i18n.en: There, of the murky earth and of misty Tartaros,

lines.text: πόντου τʼ ἀτρυγέτοιο καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος
lines.translit: pontou t' atrygetoio kai ouranou asteroentos

i18n.en: and of the barren sea and of the starry heaven,

lines.text: ἑξείης πάντων πηγαὶ καὶ πείρατʼ ἔασιν
lines.translit: hexeiēs pantōn pēgai kai peirat' easin

i18n.en: are the sources and limits of all things, in order, one after another,

lines.text: ἀργαλέʼ εὐρώεντα, τά τε στυγέουσι θεοί περ.
lines.translit: argale' eurōenta ta te stygeousi theoi per

i18n.en: grievous and dank, which even the gods abhor.

lines.text: ἔνθα δὲ μαρμάρεαί τε πύλαι καὶ χάλκεος οὐδὸς
lines.translit: entha de marmareai te pylai kai chalkeos oudos

i18n.en: There are the gleaming gates and the bronze threshold,

lines.text: ἀστεμφής, ῥίζῃσι διηνεκέεσσιν ἀρηρώς,
lines.translit: astemphēs rhizēsi diēnekeessin arērōs

i18n.en: unshaken, fixed with roots running on without end,

lines.text: αὐτοφυής· πρόσθεν δὲ θεῶν ἔκτοσθεν ἁπάντων
lines.translit: autophyēs prosthen de theōn ektosthen hapantōn

i18n.en: self-grown; and in front, apart from all the gods,

lines.text: Τιτῆνες ναίουσι, πέρην Χάεος ζοφεροῖο.
lines.translit: Titēnes naiousi perēn Chaeos zopheroio

i18n.en: the Titans dwell, beyond gloomy Chaos.

notes.official: *Τιτῆνες ναίουσι, πέρην Χάεος ζοφεροῖο* 'the Titans dwell, beyond gloomy Chaos' (814): *Χάεος* is the primordial gap/void of 116 (`chaos-primordial-chasm-void-theogony`), here a region of the underworld topography beyond which the imprisoned Titans dwell — not the later 'disorder'. Rendered 'Chaos' with Evelyn-White; *Τιτῆνες* transliterated 'Titans' (`titanes-folk-etymology-theogony`).

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἐρισμαράγοιο Διὸς κλειτοὶ ἐπίκουροι
lines.translit: autar erismaragoio Dios kleitoi epikouroi

i18n.en: But the famous helpers of loud-thundering Zeus

lines.text: δώματα ναιετάουσιν ἐπʼ Ὠκεανοῖο θεμέθλοις,
lines.translit: dōmata naietaousin ep' Ōkeanoio themethlois

i18n.en: have their dwellings upon the foundations of Okeanos,

lines.text: Κόττος τʼ ἠδὲ Γύης· Βριάρεών γε μὲν ἠὺν ἐόντα
lines.translit: Kottos t' ēde Gyēs Briareōn ge men ēyn eonta

i18n.en: Kottos and Gyes; but Briareos, being noble,

lines.text: γαμβρὸν ἑὸν ποίησε βαρύκτυπος Ἐννοσίγαιος,
lines.translit: gambron heon poiēse baryktypos Ennosigaios

i18n.en: the deep-crashing Earth-Shaker made his own son-in-law,

notes.official: *βαρύκτυπος Ἐννοσίγαιος* 'the deep-crashing Earth-Shaker' (818) is Poseidon, designated only by his periphrastic title as at 441/456 (`periphrastic-title-unnamed-god-theogony`); the noble Briareos (817) is made his son-in-law and given Kymopoleia to wed. The poem withholds the name Poseidon, and it is not supplied in the surface.

lines.text: δῶκε δὲ Κυμοπόλειαν ὀπυίειν, θυγατέρα ἥν.
lines.translit: dōke de Kymopoleian opyiein thygatera hēn

i18n.en: and gave him Kymopoleia, his daughter, to wed.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ Τιτῆνας ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐξέλασεν Ζεύς,
lines.translit: autar epei Titēnas ap' ouranou exelasen Zeus

i18n.en: But when Zeus had driven the Titans out of heaven,

notes.official: *Τυφωέα* 'Typhoeus' (820–880): after the Titans are driven from heaven, huge Gaia bears her youngest child Typhoeus in union with Tartaros (821–822) — a hundred-serpent-headed (825), fire-eyed (826–828), many-voiced (829–835) monster whom Zeus blasts with the thunderbolt and hurls into Tartaros (853–868). The surface is a plain rendering of the Greek: the serpent-anatomy at 825 under `ophis-drakon-serpent-vocabulary-theogony` (scope extended to 825), the storm-weapons under `thunder-triad-bronte-keraunos-sterope-theogony` (scope extended to 839, 845, 846, 854), Tartaros under `tartaros-underworld-vocabulary-theogony`. **Comparative apparatus (clearly labeled):** the Typhoeus-combat is the *Theogony*'s fullest instance of the Near-Eastern divine-combat / *chaoskampf* pattern (Marduk–Tiamat, Baʿlu–Yammu, YHWH–Leviathan/Rahab), documented for the Northwest/East-Semitic corpus in the central `chaoskampf-sea-conflict-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible` entry, and it echoes the Hurro-Hittite Illuyanka and Song of Ullikummi. Per the signed-off Block-A/B/C non-fusion precedent that central entry is deliberately NOT extended to any THEO refId (no THEO refId occurs in the central glossary), and the convergence — with any Wheel-of-Heaven combat-as-history reading — is confined to this note, kept out of both the surface and the philological claim. The Editor's no-central-change recommendation is in the Block-D report.

lines.text: ὁπλότατον τέκε παῖδα Τυφωέα Γαῖα πελώρη
lines.translit: hoplotaton teke paida Typhōea Gaia pelōrē

i18n.en: huge Gaia bore her youngest child, Typhoeus,

lines.text: Ταρτάρου ἐν φιλότητι διὰ χρυσέην Ἀφροδίτην·
lines.translit: Tartarou en philotēti dia chryseēn Aphroditēn

i18n.en: in love with Tartaros, through golden Aphrodite;

lines.text: οὗ χεῖρες μὲν ἔασιν ἐπʼ ἰσχύι, ἔργματʼ ἔχουσαι,
lines.translit: hou cheires men easin ep' ischyi ergmat' echousai

i18n.en: whose hands were strong for deeds,

lines.text: καὶ πόδες ἀκάματοι κρατεροῦ θεοῦ· ἐκ δέ οἱ ὤμων
lines.translit: kai podes akamatoi kraterou theou ek de hoi ōmōn

i18n.en: and the feet of the mighty god were untiring; and from his shoulders

lines.text: ἣν ἑκατὸν κεφαλαὶ ὄφιος, δεινοῖο δράκοντος,
lines.translit: hēn hekaton kephalai ophios deinoio drakontos

i18n.en: there were a hundred heads of a serpent, a dread dragon,

notes.official: *ἣν ἑκατὸν κεφαλαὶ ὄφιος, δεινοῖο δράκοντος* 'a hundred heads of a serpent, a dread dragon' (825): *ὄφις* 'serpent' and *δράκων* 'serpent/dragon' are used of the one creature, as in the Echidna–Chimaira sequence (299, 322–323, 334), with no fixed technical opposition (LSJ; the reference varies 'serpent'/'dragon' by context). Rendered accordingly; `ophis-drakon-serpent-vocabulary-theogony`, scope extended from the Block-B monster-catalogue to the poem's climactic serpent.

lines.text: γλώσσῃσιν δνοφερῇσι λελιχμότες, ἐκ δέ οἱ ὄσσων
lines.translit: glōssēsin dnopherēsi lelichmotes ek de hoi ossōn

i18n.en: flickering with dark tongues; and from the eyes

lines.text: θεσπεσίῃς κεφαλῇσιν ὑπʼ ὀφρύσι πῦρ ἀμάρυσσεν·
lines.translit: thespesiēs kephalēsin hyp' ophrysi pyr amaryssen

i18n.en: in his wondrous heads fire sparkled beneath the brows;

lines.text: πασέων δʼ ἐκ κεφαλέων πῦρ καίετο δερκομένοιο·
lines.translit: paseōn d' ek kephaleōn pyr kaieto derkomenoio

i18n.en: and from all his heads fire burned as he glared.

lines.text: φωναὶ δʼ ἐν πάσῃσιν ἔσαν δεινῇς κεφαλῇσι
lines.translit: phōnai d' en pasēsin esan deinēs kephalēsi

i18n.en: And there were voices in all his dreadful heads,

lines.text: παντοίην ὄπʼ ἰεῖσαι ἀθέσφατον· ἄλλοτε μὲν γὰρ
lines.translit: pantoiēn op' ieisai athesphaton allote men gar

i18n.en: sending forth all kinds of unspeakable sound; for at one time

lines.text: φθέγγονθʼ ὥστε θεοῖσι συνιέμεν, ἄλλοτε δʼ αὖτε
lines.translit: phthengonth' hōste theoisi syniemen allote d' aute

i18n.en: they uttered speech such that the gods could understand, and at another

lines.text: ταύρου ἐριβρύχεω, μένος ἀσχέτου, ὄσσαν ἀγαύρου,
lines.translit: taurou eribrycheō menos aschetou ossan agaurou

i18n.en: the cry of a loud-bellowing bull, unrestrained in fury, proud of voice;

lines.text: ἄλλοτε δʼ αὖτε λέοντος ἀναιδέα θυμὸν ἔχοντος,
lines.translit: allote d' aute leontos anaidea thymon echontos

i18n.en: and at another the voice of a lion with a ruthless heart;

lines.text: ἄλλοτε δʼ αὖ σκυλάκεσσιν ἐοικότα, θαύματʼ ἀκοῦσαι,
lines.translit: allote d' au skylakessin eoikota thaumat' akousai

i18n.en: and at another sounds like whelps, a wonder to hear;

lines.text: ἄλλοτε δʼ αὖ ῥοίζεσχʼ, ὑπὸ δʼ ἤχεεν οὔρεα μακρά.
lines.translit: allote d' au rhoizesch' hypo d' ēcheen ourea makra

i18n.en: and at another he hissed, and the high mountains echoed beneath.

lines.text: καί νύ κεν ἔπλετο ἔργον ἀμήχανον ἤματι κείνῳ
lines.translit: kai ny ken epleto ergon amēchanon ēmati keinō

i18n.en: And on that day a deed beyond remedy would have come to pass,

lines.text: καί κεν ὅ γε θνητοῖσι καὶ ἀθανάτοισιν ἄναξεν,
lines.translit: kai ken ho ge thnētoisi kai athanatoisin anaxen

i18n.en: and he would have ruled over mortals and immortals,

lines.text: εἰ μὴ ἄρʼ ὀξὺ νόησε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε.
lines.translit: ei mē ar' oxy noēse patēr andrōn te theōn te

i18n.en: had not the father of men and gods sharply perceived it.

lines.text: σκληρὸν δʼ ἐβρόντησε καὶ ὄβριμον, ἀμφὶ δὲ γαῖα
lines.translit: sklēron d' ebrontēse kai obrimon amphi de gaia

i18n.en: Harshly and mightily he thundered, and round about the earth

notes.official: *ἐβρόντησε* 'he thundered' (839), with *βροντή/στεροπή/κεραυνός* recurring at 845–846 and 854: Zeus's storm-triad, first given by the Kyklopes (504–505, Block C) and decisive in the Titanomachy (690–708), now deployed against Typhoeus. Rendered 'thunder / lightning / (blazing) thunderbolt' consistently with Evelyn-White, without a rigid technical distinction the poem does not mark; `thunder-triad-bronte-keraunos-sterope-theogony`, scope extended to 839, 845, 846, 854.

lines.text: σμερδαλέον κονάβησε καὶ οὐρανὸς εὐρὺς ὕπερθε
lines.translit: smerdaleon konabēse kai ouranos eurys hyperthe

i18n.en: rang terribly, and the wide heaven above,

lines.text: πόντος τʼ Ὠκεανοῦ τε ῥοαὶ καὶ Τάρταρα γαίης.
lines.translit: pontos t' Ōkeanou te rhoai kai Tartara gaiēs

i18n.en: and the sea, and the streams of Okeanos, and the nether pit of the earth.

lines.text: ποσσὶ δʼ ὕπʼ ἀθανάτοισι μέγας πελεμίζετʼ Ὄλυμπος
lines.translit: possi d' hyp' athanatoisi megas pelemizet' Olympos

i18n.en: Great Olympos trembled beneath the immortal feet

lines.text: ὀρνυμένοιο ἄνακτος· ἐπεστενάχιζε δὲ γαῖα.
lines.translit: ornymenoio anaktos epestenachize de gaia

i18n.en: of the lord as he rose; and the earth groaned.

lines.text: καῦμα δʼ ὑπʼ ἀμφοτέρων κάτεχεν ἰοειδέα πόντον
lines.translit: kauma d' hyp' amphoterōn katechen ioeidea ponton

i18n.en: A burning heat from both of them seized the violet-dark sea,

lines.text: βροντῆς τε στεροπῆς τε, πυρός τʼ ἀπὸ τοῖο πελώρου,
lines.translit: brontēs te steropēs te pyros t' apo toio pelōrou

i18n.en: from the thunder and the lightning, and the fire from that monster,

lines.text: πρηστήρων ἀνέμων τε κεραυνοῦ τε φλεγέθοντος.
lines.translit: prēstērōn anemōn te keraunou te phlegethontos

i18n.en: from the scorching whirlwinds and the blazing thunderbolt.

lines.text: ἔζεε δὲ χθὼν πᾶσα καὶ οὐρανὸς ἠδὲ θάλασσα·
lines.translit: ezee de chthōn pasa kai ouranos ēde thalassa

i18n.en: The whole earth boiled, and the heaven and the sea;

lines.text: θυῖε δʼ ἄρʼ ἀμφʼ ἀκτὰς περί τʼ ἀμφί τε κύματα μακρὰ
lines.translit: thyie d' ar' amph' aktas peri t' amphi te kymata makra

i18n.en: and long waves raged about the shores, around and around,

lines.text: ῥιπῇ ὕπʼ ἀθανάτων, ἔνοσις δʼ ἄσβεστος ὀρώρει·
lines.translit: rhipē hyp' athanatōn enosis d' asbestos orōrei

i18n.en: beneath the onrush of the immortals, and an unquenchable quaking arose.

lines.text: τρέε δʼ Ἀίδης, ἐνέροισι καταφθιμένοισιν ἀνάσσων,
lines.translit: tree d' Aidēs eneroisi kataphthimenoisin anassōn

i18n.en: Hades trembled, who rules over the dead below,

lines.text: Τιτῆνές θʼ ὑποταρτάριοι, Κρόνον ἀμφὶς ἐόντες,
lines.translit: Titēnes th' hypotartarioi Kronon amphis eontes

i18n.en: and the Titans beneath Tartaros, gathered about Kronos,

lines.text: ἀσβέστου κελάδοιο καὶ αἰνῆς δηιοτῆτος.
lines.translit: asbestou keladoio kai ainēs dēiotētos

i18n.en: at the unquenchable din and the terrible fray.

lines.text: Ζεὺς δʼ ἐπεὶ οὖν κόρθυνεν ἑὸν μένος, εἵλετο δʼ ὅπλα,
lines.translit: Zeus d' epei oun korthynen heon menos heileto d' hopla

i18n.en: But when Zeus had gathered up his strength and seized his weapons,

lines.text: βροντήν τε στεροπήν τε καὶ αἰθαλόεντα κεραυνόν,
lines.translit: brontēn te steropēn te kai aithaloenta keraunon

i18n.en: thunder and lightning and the blazing thunderbolt,

lines.text: πλῆξεν ἀπʼ Οὐλύμποιο ἐπάλμενος· ἀμφὶ δὲ πάσας
lines.translit: plēxen ap' Oulympoio epalmenos amphi de pasas

i18n.en: he leaped and struck from Olympos; and all around

notes.official: *ἀπʼ Οὐλύμποιο* (855; again *ἐν Οὐλύμπῳ* 953): the epic diectatic *Οὔλυμπ-* is normalized to the standard Greek form 'Olympos' in the surface (as already at 397, Block C), the source spelling kept verbatim in the text field; 'Olympos' is the Greek form, not the Latinized 'Olympus'. Governed by `place-name-greek-forms-block-c-theogony`, whose place-name normalization convention is extended to the Block-D toponyms (Olympos 855/953, Krete 971, Iolkos 997).

lines.text: ἔπρεσε θεσπεσίας κεφαλὰς δεινοῖο πελώρου.
lines.translit: eprese thespesias kephalas deinoio pelōrou

i18n.en: he scorched the wondrous heads of the dread monster.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ δή μιν δάμασεν πληγῇσιν ἱμάσσας,
lines.translit: autar epei dē min damasen plēgēsin himassas

i18n.en: But when he had overpowered him, lashing him with blows,

lines.text: ἤριπε γυιωθείς, στενάχιζε δὲ γαῖα πελώρη.
lines.translit: ēripe gyiōtheis stenachize de gaia pelōrē

i18n.en: he fell down crippled, and the huge earth groaned.

lines.text: φλὸξ δὲ κεραυνωθέντος ἀπέσσυτο τοῖο ἄνακτος
lines.translit: phlox de keraunōthentos apessyto toio anaktos

i18n.en: And a flame shot forth from that lord when he was struck by the thunderbolt,

lines.text: οὔρεος ἐν βήσσῃσιν ἀιδνῇς παιπαλοέσσῃς,
lines.translit: oureos en bēssēsin aidnēs paipaloessēs

i18n.en: in the dark, rugged glens of the mountain,

lines.text: πληγέντος. πολλὴ δὲ πελώρη καίετο γαῖα
lines.translit: plēgentos pollē de pelōrē kaieto gaia

i18n.en: where he was smitten. And a great part of the huge earth was scorched

lines.text: ἀτμῇ θεσπεσίῃ καὶ ἐτήκετο κασσίτερος ὣς
lines.translit: atmē thespesiē kai etēketo kassiteros hōs

i18n.en: by the wondrous blast, and melted like tin

lines.text: τέχνῃ ὕπʼ αἰζηῶν ἐν ἐυτρήτοις χοάνοισι
lines.translit: technē hyp' aizēōn en eutrētois choanoisi

i18n.en: heated by the craft of young men in well-bored crucibles,

lines.text: θαλφθείς, ἠὲ σίδηρος, ὅ περ κρατερώτατός ἐστιν.
lines.translit: thalphtheis ēe sidēros ho per kraterōtatos estin

i18n.en: or like iron, which is the strongest of all things,

lines.text: οὔρεος ἐν βήσσῃσι δαμαζόμενος πυρὶ κηλέῳ
lines.translit: oureos en bēssēsi damazomenos pyri kēleō

i18n.en: subdued in the mountain glens by blazing fire

lines.text: τήκεται ἐν χθονὶ δίῃ ὑφʼ Ἡφαιστου παλάμῃσιν.
lines.translit: tēketai en chthoni diē hyph' Hēphaistou palamēsin

i18n.en: and melts in the bright earth beneath the hands of Hephaestus.

lines.text: ὣς ἄρα τήκετο γαῖα σέλαι πυρὸς αἰθομένοιο.
lines.translit: hōs ara tēketo gaia selai pyros aithomenoio

i18n.en: So the earth melted in the glow of the blazing fire.

lines.text: ῥῖψε δέ μιν θυμῷ ἀκαχὼν ἐς Τάρταρον εὐρύν.
lines.translit: rhipse de min thymō akachōn es Tartaron euryn

i18n.en: And he hurled him, grieved in his heart, into wide Tartaros.

lines.text: ἐκ δὲ Τυφωέος ἔστʼ ἀνέμων μένος ὑγρὸν ἀέντων,
lines.translit: ek de Typhōeos est' anemōn menos hygron aentōn

i18n.en: And from Typhoeus comes the might of the wet winds that blow,

notes.official: *ἐκ δὲ Τυφωέος … ἀνέμων μένος* 'from Typhoeus comes the might of the … winds' (869–880): the destructive storm-winds are aetiologically derived from the blasted monster, held apart from the beneficial named winds *Νότος/Βορέης/Ζέφυρος* Notos, Boreas, Zephyros (870), who are 'of the race of the gods' (871). Rendered literally with Evelyn-White; the wind-names transliterated per the name convention.

lines.text: νόσφι Νότου Βορέω τε καὶ ἀργέστεω Ζεφύροιο·
lines.translit: nosphi Notou Boreō te kai argesteō Zephyroio

i18n.en: apart from Notos and Boreas and the clearing Zephyros;

lines.text: οἵ γε μὲν ἐκ θεόφιν γενεή, θνητοῖς μέγʼ ὄνειαρ·
lines.translit: hoi ge men ek theophin geneē thnētois meg' oneiar

i18n.en: these are of the race of the gods, a great boon to mortals;

lines.text: οἱ δʼ ἄλλοι μαψαῦραι ἐπιπνείουσι θάλασσαν·
lines.translit: hoi d' alloi mapsaurai epipneiousi thalassan

i18n.en: but the others, the idle gusts, blow over the sea.

lines.text: αἳ δή τοι πίπτουσαι ἐς ἠεροειδέα πόντον,
lines.translit: hai dē toi piptousai es ēeroeidea ponton

i18n.en: These, falling upon the misty sea,

lines.text: πῆμα μέγα θνητοῖσι, κακῇ θυίουσιν ἀέλλῃ·
lines.translit: pēma mega thnētoisi kakē thyiousin aellē

i18n.en: a great bane to mortals, rage with an evil storm;

lines.text: ἄλλοτε δʼ ἄλλαι ἄεισι διασκιδνᾶσί τε νῆας
lines.translit: allote d' allai aeisi diaskidnasi te nēas

i18n.en: at different times they blow different ways, and scatter ships

lines.text: ναύτας τε φθείρουσι· κακοῦ δʼ οὐ γίγνεται ἀλκὴ
lines.translit: nautas te phtheirousi kakou d' ou gignetai alkē

i18n.en: and destroy sailors; and there is no defense against the evil

lines.text: ἀνδράσιν, οἳ κείνῃσι συνάντωνται κατὰ πόντον·
lines.translit: andrasin hoi keinēsi synantōntai kata ponton

i18n.en: for men who meet with them upon the sea.

lines.text: αἳ δʼ αὖ καὶ κατὰ γαῖαν ἀπείριτον ἀνθεμόεσσαν
lines.translit: hai d' au kai kata gaian apeiriton anthemoessan

i18n.en: And again, over the boundless flowering earth

lines.text: ἔργʼ ἐρατὰ φθείρουσι χαμαιγενέων ἀνθρώπων
lines.translit: erg' erata phtheirousi chamaigeneōn anthrōpōn

i18n.en: they ruin the lovely works of earth-born men,

lines.text: πιμπλεῖσαι κόνιός τε καὶ ἀργαλέου κολοσυρτοῦ.
lines.translit: pimpleisai konios te kai argaleou kolosyrtou

i18n.en: filling them with dust and grievous confusion.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί ῥα πόνον μάκαρες θεοὶ ἐξετέλεσσαν,
lines.translit: autar epei rha ponon makares theoi exetelessan

i18n.en: But when the blessed gods had finished their toil,

lines.text: Τιτήνεσσι δὲ τιμάων κρίναντο βίηφι,
lines.translit: Titēnessi de timaōn krinanto biēphi

i18n.en: and by force had settled with the Titans the matter of their honors,

notes.official: *Τιτήνεσσι … τιμάων κρίναντο βίηφι* 'by force they settled with the Titans the matter of their honours' (882), and Zeus *ἑὰς διεδάσσατο τιμάς* 'distributed among them their honours' (885): the apportioned-honour lexicon (*τιμή/τιμαί*) of the accession-offer and the Hekate hymn (392–449, Block B) reaches its structural payoff as Zeus, made king *Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσιν* 'by the counsels of Gaia' (884), divides the *timai* among the gods. Rendered 'honours' consistently with Evelyn-White; `time-geras-moira-honor-vocabulary-theogony`, scope extended from the Hekate hymn (≤449) to its accession payoff 882, 885, 892, 904. **Lens-discipline note:** a sovereign distributing offices/domains is a WoH-salient theme, but surface and note stay lexical and press no canon mapping.

lines.text: δή ῥα τότʼ ὤτρυνον βασιλευέμεν ἠδὲ ἀνάσσειν
lines.translit: dē rha tot' ōtrynon basileuemen ēde anassein

i18n.en: then indeed they urged him to be king and to rule—

lines.text: Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσιν Ὀλύμπιον εὐρύοπα Ζῆν
lines.translit: Gaiēs phradmosynēsin Olympion euryopa Zēn

i18n.en: by the counsels of Gaia—wide-seeing Olympian Zeus,

notes.official: *Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσιν* 'by the counsels of Gaia' (884), restated at 891 (*Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσι καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος*): the culmination of the Gaia-counsel motif tracked since Block C — Gaia and Ouranos' prophecy to Kronos (463–465, 475), the *ἐννεσίαι* that make Kronos disgorge (494), the *φραδμοσύναι* that raise the Hundred-Handers (626). Here her counsel installs Zeus as king (884) and prompts the swallowing of Metis (891), completing the succession the motif has driven throughout. Rendered 'the counsels of Gaia' with Evelyn-White; `gaia-counsel-prophecy-vocabulary-theogony`, scope extended from ≤626 to its Block-D culmination 884, 891. **Lens-discipline note:** Gaia as the earth-power whose foreknowledge steers each regime-change is WoH-salient, but both surface and note stay at the lexical level and press no cosmological reading.

lines.text: ἀθανάτων· ὃ δὲ τοῖσιν ἑὰς διεδάσσατο τιμάς.
lines.translit: athanatōn ho de toisin heas diedassato timas

i18n.en: over the immortals; and he distributed among them their honors.

lines.text: Ζεὺς δὲ θεῶν βασιλεὺς πρώτην ἄλοχον θέτο Μῆτιν
lines.translit: Zeus de theōn basileus prōtēn alochon theto Mētin

i18n.en: Now Zeus, king of the gods, made Metis his first wife,

notes.official: *Μῆτιν* 'Metis' (886), Zeus's first wife, *πλεῖστα … ἰδυῖαν* 'who knows most' (887): her name is the noun *μῆτις* 'cunning counsel, cleverness', and the episode turns on the pun — Zeus swallows Metis to forestall a stronger son (891–900) and thereby internalizes *mētis* itself, becoming *μητίετα Ζεύς* 'Zeus the counsellor' (904, 914). The name is transliterated 'Metis' (not glossed inline 'Cunning'), *μητίετα* rendered 'the counsellor' with Evelyn-White (as at 520); the *mētis* network — including the etymological tie to Kronos's epithet *ἀγκυλομήτης* 'of crooked counsel' (18/137/168/473/495, the crooked-counselled father whom the counsellor-son now outdoes) — is carried in commentary and the new `metis-metieta-cunning-counsel-network-theogony` entry, not in the surface. **Cross-corpus note:** the Metis-swallowing (a sovereign absorbing the counsel-goddess) is kept distinct from the Mesopotamian/Hebrew wisdom entries in the central glossary; non-fusion, per the Block-D report.

lines.text: πλεῖστα τε ἰδυῖαν ἰδὲ θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων.
lines.translit: pleista te idyian ide thnētōn anthrōpōn

i18n.en: she who knows most of gods and of mortal men.

notes.official: The printed Perseus line is hypometric: *πλεῖστα τε ἰδυῖαν ἰδὲ θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων* omits *θεῶν*, which the standard text carries (cf. West ad 886–900 and the doublet at 929p, *πλεῖστα θεῶν εἰδυῖαν ἰδὲ θνητῶν ἀνθρώπων*). The surface follows the standard text, 'of gods and of mortal men'; the defective printed line is preserved verbatim in the text field per the source-immutability policy, governed by `source-orthographic-quirks-verbatim-theogony`.

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ὅτε δὴ ἄρʼ ἔμελλε θεὰν γλαυκῶπιν Ἀθήνην
lines.translit: all' hote dē ar' emelle thean glaukōpin Athēnēn

i18n.en: But when she was about to bring forth the bright-eyed goddess Athena,

lines.text: τέξεσθαι, τότʼ ἔπειτα δόλῳ φρένας ἐξαπατήσας
lines.translit: texesthai tot' epeita dolō phrenas exapatēsas

i18n.en: then, deceiving her wits by craft

lines.text: αἱμυλίοισι λόγοισιν ἑὴν ἐσκάτθετο νηδὺν
lines.translit: haimylioisi logoisin heēn eskattheto nēdyn

i18n.en: with wheedling words, he put her into his own belly,

lines.text: Γαίης φραδμοσύνῃσι καὶ Οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος.
lines.translit: Gaiēs phradmosynēsi kai Ouranou asteroentos

i18n.en: by the counsels of Gaia and of starry Ouranos.

lines.text: τὼς γάρ οἱ φρασάτην, ἵνα μὴ βασιληίδα τιμὴν
lines.translit: tōs gar hoi phrasatēn hina mē basilēida timēn

i18n.en: For thus they counseled him, so that no other of the eternal gods

lines.text: ἄλλος ἔχοι Διὸς ἀντὶ θεῶν αἰειγενετάων.
lines.translit: allos echoi Dios anti theōn aieigenetaōn

i18n.en: should hold the kingly honor in place of Zeus.

lines.text: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς εἵμαρτο περίφρονα τέκνα γενέσθαι·
lines.translit: ek gar tēs heimarto periphrona tekna genesthai

i18n.en: For from her it was fated that wise children should be born:

lines.text: πρώτην μὲν κούρην γλαυκώπιδα Τριτογένειαν
lines.translit: prōtēn men kourēn glaukōpida Tritogeneian

i18n.en: first a maiden, bright-eyed Tritogeneia,

notes.official: *Τριτογένειαν* 'Tritogeneia' (895, again 924): a cult-epithet of Athena of contested sense ('Trito-born', variously linked to Lake Tritonis or an obscure *tritō-*), transliterated as a name with Evelyn-White rather than etymologized. The fated children of Metis are first this *κούρη* with strength equal to her father's (895–896), then the son who never comes (897–900), forestalled by the swallowing. Name convention.

lines.text: ἶσον ἔχουσαν πατρὶ μένος καὶ ἐπίφρονα βουλήν.
lines.translit: ison echousan patri menos kai epiphrona boulēn

i18n.en: having strength equal to her father's and prudent counsel;

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ἔπειτʼ ἄρα παῖδα θεῶν βασιλῆα καὶ ἀνδρῶν
lines.translit: autar epeit' ara paida theōn basilēa kai andrōn

i18n.en: but afterward she was to bear a son, king of gods and men,

lines.text: ἤμελλεν τέξεσθαι, ὑπέρβιον ἦτορ ἔχοντα·
lines.translit: ēmellen texesthai hyperbion ētor echonta

i18n.en: with an overbearing heart.

lines.text: ἀλλʼ ἄρα μιν Ζεὺς πρόσθεν ἑὴν ἐσκάτθετο νηδύν,
lines.translit: all' ara min Zeus prosthen heēn eskattheto nēdyn

i18n.en: But Zeus put her first into his own belly,

lines.text: ὡς δή οἱ φράσσαιτο θεὰ ἀγαθόν τε κακόν τε.
lines.translit: hōs dē hoi phrassaito thea agathon te kakon te

i18n.en: so that the goddess might advise him of good and evil.

lines.text: δεύτερον ἠγάγετο λιπαρὴν Θέμιν, ἣ τέκεν Ὥρας,
lines.translit: deuteron ēgageto liparēn Themin hē teken Hōras

i18n.en: Next he wedded bright Themis, who bore the Horai—

lines.text: Εὐνουμίην τε Δίκην τε καὶ Εἰρήνην τεθαλυῖαν,
lines.translit: Eunomiēn te Dikēn te kai Eirēnēn tethalyian

i18n.en: Eunomia and Dike and blooming Eirene,

notes.official: *Ὥρας* 'the Horai' (901) and their names *Εὐνομίην τε Δίκην τε καὶ Εἰρήνην* (902): transparent personified abstractions — Eunomia 'Good-order/Lawfulness', Dike 'Justice', Eirene 'Peace' — that also function as the named Seasons-goddesses. Following the reference and by the principle of `personified-abstractions-nyx-eris-brood-theogony` (translate running abstractions, transliterate cult-established name-like members), they are transliterated as proper names, exactly like their sisters the Charites Aglaia/Euphrosyne/Thalia (909); the transparent senses are given here, not glossed inline in the surface, which is governed by the name convention. The source prints *Εὐνουμίην* (902); the transmitted spelling is kept verbatim in the text field, the standard 'Eunomia' in the transliteration and English (`source-orthographic-quirks-verbatim-theogony`).

lines.text: αἳ ἔργʼ ὠρεύουσι καταθνητοῖσι βροτοῖσι,
lines.translit: hai erg' ōreuousi katathnētoisi brotoisi

i18n.en: who watch over the works of mortal men—

lines.text: Μοίρας θʼ, ᾗ πλείστην τιμὴν πόρε μητίετα Ζεύς,
lines.translit: Moiras th' hē pleistēn timēn pore mētieta Zeus

i18n.en: and the Fates, to whom Zeus the counsellor gave the greatest honor,

notes.official: *Μοίρας* 'the Fates' (904), with *Κλωθώ τε Λάχεσίν τε καὶ Ἄτροπον* (905): here daughters of Zeus and Themis — a genealogical doublet of the Moirai born within Nyx's parthenogenetic brood at 211/217 (a known Hesiodic inconsistency, two parentages for the same powers; West 1966 ad 904). The individual names Klotho/Lachesis/Atropos are transliterated exactly as at 218 (`personified-abstractions-nyx-eris-brood-theogony`); the collective *Μοίρας* is rendered 'the Fates' (standing alone), as against 'the Destinies' at 217, where it was paired with the *Κῆρας* 'Fates' and needed a distinguishing English word. To them *μητίετα* 'the counsellor' Zeus gave *πλείστην τιμήν* 'the greatest honour' (904) — *timḗ* under `time-geras-moira-honor-vocabulary-theogony`, *mētieta* under `metis-metieta-cunning-counsel-network-theogony`. The personified-abstractions entry is not extended into this Themis catalogue; the doublet is flagged here.

lines.text: Κλωθώ τε Λάχεσίν τε καὶ Ἄτροπον, αἵτε διδοῦσι
lines.translit: Klōthō te Lachesin te kai Atropon haite didousi

i18n.en: Klotho and Lachesis and Atropos, who give

lines.text: θνητοῖς ἀνθρώποισιν ἔχειν ἀγαθόν τε κακόν τε.
lines.translit: thnētois anthrōpoisin echein agathon te kakon te

i18n.en: to mortal men both good and evil to have.

lines.text: τρεῖς δέ οἱ Εὐρυνομη Χάριτας τέκε καλλιπαρῄους,
lines.translit: treis de hoi Eurynomē Charitas teke kalliparēous

i18n.en: And Eurynome bore him the three fair-cheeked Graces—

notes.official: *Εὐρυνόμη* 'Eurynome', the Okeanid mother of the three Charites (907–909): the source prints the name without its accent (*Εὐρυνομη*). The transmitted spelling is kept verbatim in the text field and the standard 'Eurynome' given in the transliteration and English, per the source-fidelity convention (`source-orthographic-quirks-verbatim-theogony`; cf. the unaccented *Χρυσαωρ* at 281).

lines.text: Ὠκεανοῦ κούρη, πολυήρατον εἶδος ἔχουσα,
lines.translit: Ōkeanou kourē polyēraton eidos echousa

i18n.en: daughter of Okeanos, having a lovely form—

lines.text: Ἀγλαΐην τε καὶ Εὐφροσύνην Θαλίην τʼ ἐρατεινήν·
lines.translit: Aglaiēn te kai Euphrosynēn Thaliēn t' erateinēn

i18n.en: Aglaia and Euphrosyne and lovely Thalia;

lines.text: τῶν καὶ ἀπὸ βλεφάρων ἔρος εἴβετο δερκομενάων
lines.translit: tōn kai apo blepharōn eros eibeto derkomenaōn

i18n.en: and from their eyes, as they glanced, desire flowed,

lines.text: λυσιμελής· καλὸν δέ θʼ ὑπʼ ὀφρύσι δερκιόωνται.
lines.translit: lysimelēs kalon de th' hyp' ophrysi derkioōntai

i18n.en: desire that loosens the limbs; and beautifully they glance from beneath their brows.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ὁ Δήμητρος πολυφόρβης ἐς λέχος ἦλθεν,
lines.translit: autar ho Dēmētros polyphorbēs es lechos ēlthen

i18n.en: But he came to the bed of all-nourishing Demeter,

lines.text: ἣ τέκε Περσεφόνην λευκώλενον, ἣν Ἀιδωνεὺς
lines.translit: hē teke Persephonēn leukōlenon hēn Aidōneus

i18n.en: who bore white-armed Persephone, whom Aidoneus

notes.official: *Ἀιδωνεύς* 'Aidoneus' (913), who carries off Persephone: a fuller alternative name of Hades (an expanded epic form), NOT a mere orthographic variant of *Ἅιδης*. It is therefore kept as 'Aidoneus' with Evelyn-White and deliberately NOT normalized to 'Hades' — unlike the plain epic *Ἀίδης/Ἀίδεω* forms at 768/774/850, which the `dialectal-theonym-normalization-theogony` convention does normalize. Governed by the name convention; the non-normalization is flagged in the Block-D report.

lines.text: ἥρπασε ἧς παρὰ μητρός· ἔδωκε δὲ μητίετα Ζεύς.
lines.translit: hērpase hēs para mētros edōke de mētieta Zeus

i18n.en: carried off from her mother; and Zeus the counsellor gave her.

lines.text: Μνημοσύνης δʼ ἐξαῦτις ἐράσσατο καλλικόμοιο,
lines.translit: Mnēmosynēs d' exautis erassato kallikomoio

i18n.en: And again he loved fair-haired Mnemosyne,

lines.text: ἐξ ἧς οἱ Μοῦσαι χρυσάμπυκες ἐξεγένοντο
lines.translit: ex hēs hoi Mousai chrysampykes exegenonto

i18n.en: from whom the gold-filleted Muses were born to him,

lines.text: ἐννέα, τῇσιν ἅδον θαλίαι καὶ τέρψις ἀοιδῆς.
lines.translit: ennea tēsin hadon thaliai kai terpsis aoidēs

i18n.en: nine of them, to whom festivities and the delight of song are dear.

lines.text: Λητὼ δʼ Ἀπόλλωνα καὶ Ἄρτεμιν ἰοχέαιραν,
lines.translit: Lētō d' Apollōna kai Artemin iocheairan

i18n.en: And Leto bore Apollo and Artemis, delighting in arrows,

lines.text: ἱμερόεντα γόνον περὶ πάντων Οὐρανιώνων,
lines.translit: himeroenta gonon peri pantōn Ouraniōnōn

i18n.en: offspring lovelier than all the children of Heaven,

lines.text: γείνατʼ ἄρʼ αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς φιλότητι μιγεῖσα.
lines.translit: geinat' ar' aigiochoio Dios philotēti migeisa

i18n.en: having mingled in love with aegis-holding Zeus.

lines.text: λοισθοτάτην δʼ Ἥρην θαλερὴν ποιήσατʼ ἄκοιτιν·
lines.translit: loisthotatēn d' Hērēn thalerēn poiēsat' akoitin

i18n.en: And last of all he made blooming Hera his wife;

lines.text: ἣ δʼ Ἥβην καὶ Ἄρηα καὶ Εἰλείθυιαν ἔτικτε
lines.translit: hē d' Hēbēn kai Arēa kai Eileithyian etikte

i18n.en: and she bore Hebe and Ares and Eileithyia,

lines.text: μιχθεῖσʼ ἐν φιλότητι θεῶν βασιλῆι καὶ ἀνδρῶν.
lines.translit: michtheis' en philotēti theōn basilēi kai andrōn

i18n.en: mingling in love with the king of gods and men.

lines.text: αὐτὸς δʼ ἐκ κεφαλῆς γλαυκώπιδα Τριτογένειαν
lines.translit: autos d' ek kephalēs glaukōpida Tritogeneian

i18n.en: But he himself, from his head, brought forth bright-eyed Tritogeneia,

notes.official: *αὐτὸς δʼ ἐκ κεφαλῆς … Τριτογένειαν* 'he himself, from his head, brought forth Tritogeneia' (924–926): the birth of Athena directly from Zeus, the swallowing of Metis (886–900, and the variant 929e–t) having transferred her *mētis* to him. *Ἀτρυτώνην* 'Atrytone' ('unwearying', 925) and *Τριτογένειαν* transliterated as cult-epithets with Evelyn-White. See on 886 and the variant-passage note at 929a.

lines.text: δεινὴν ἐγρεκύδοιμον ἀγέστρατον Ἀτρυτώνην
lines.translit: deinēn egrekydoimon agestraton Atrytōnēn

i18n.en: the dread rouser of the war-din, leader of armies, Atrytone,

lines.text: πότνιαν, ᾗ κέλαδοί τε ἅδον πόλεμοί τε μάχαι τε,
lines.translit: potnian hē keladoi te hadon polemoi te machai te

i18n.en: the lady to whom din and wars and battles are dear;

lines.text: Ἥρη δʼ Ἥφαιστον κλυτὸν οὐ φιλότητι μιγεῖσα
lines.translit: Hērē d' Hēphaiston klyton ou philotēti migeisa

i18n.en: and Hera bore glorious Hephaestus, not mingling in love,

lines.text: γείνατο, καὶ ζαμένησε καὶ ἤρισε ᾧ παρακοίτῃ,
lines.translit: geinato kai zamenēse kai ērise hō parakoitē

i18n.en: but in wrath and quarrel with her husband,

lines.text: ἐκ πάντων τέχνῃσι κεκασμένον Οὐρανιώνων.
lines.translit: ek pantōn technēsi kekasmenon Ouraniōnōn

i18n.en: Hephaestus, skilled in crafts beyond all the children of Heaven.

lines.text: Ἥρη δὲ ζαμένησε καὶ ἤρισε ᾧ παρακοίτῃ.
lines.translit: Hērē de zamenēse kai ērise hō parakoitē

i18n.en: But Hera was wroth and quarreled with her husband,

notes.official: Lines 929a–929t are a twenty-line variant/doublet transmitted by Chrysippus (apud Galen, *De placitis Hippocratis et Platonis* 3.8) and printed by the Perseus/West edition as an *<add>* supplement in source order after 929; West brackets the whole block as secondary. It re-tells, in a fuller form, Hera's parthenogenesis of Hephaestus 'in strife' (929a–d, doublet of 927–929) and the deception and swallowing of Metis and the birth of Athena (929e–t, doublet of 886–900 + 924), locating Athena's birth by the river Triton (929m). Per the presentation decision adopted for the block — an extension of the athetized-lines philosophy from single *<del>* lines to an *<add>* supplement — the passage is retained and translated verbatim in source order, unmarked in the reading surface, with its supplementary/doublet status recorded here and the additional internal athetesis of 929s recorded at that line; see the new `variant-passage-929a-929t-metis-doublet-theogony` entry. **Flagged for the Reviewer:** the passage-level presentation (retain-and-translate-unmarked versus any stronger apparatus marking of the whole block) is the block's principal apparatus adjudication.

lines.text: ἐκ ταύτης δʼ ἔριδος ἣ μὲν τέκε φαίδιμον υἱὸν
lines.translit: ek tautēs d' eridos hē men teke phaidimon huion

i18n.en: and out of this strife she bore a glorious son,

lines.text: Ἥφαιστον, φιλότητος ἄτερ Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο,
lines.translit: Hēphaiston philotētos ater Dios aigiochoio

i18n.en: Hephaestus, apart from the love of aegis-holding Zeus,

lines.text: ἐκ πάντων παλάμῃσι κεκασμένον Οὐρανιώνων·
lines.translit: ek pantōn palamēsi kekasmenon Ouraniōnōn

i18n.en: skilled with his hands beyond all the children of Heaven.

lines.text: αὐτὰρ ὅ γʼ Ὠκεανοῦ καὶ Τηθύος ἠυκόμοιο
lines.translit: autar ho g' Ōkeanou kai Tēthyos ēykomoio

i18n.en: But he himself lay beside the daughter of Okeanos and fair-haired Tethys,

lines.text: κούρῃ νόσφʼ Ἥρης παρελέξατο καλλιπαρήῳ,
lines.translit: kourē nosph' Hērēs parelexato kalliparēō

i18n.en: the fair-cheeked maiden, apart from Hera—

lines.text: ἐξαπαφὼν Μῆτιν καίπερ πολυδήνεʼ ἐοῦσαν.
lines.translit: exapaphōn Mētin kaiper polydēne' eousan

i18n.en: deceiving Metis, though she was full of cunning.

lines.text: συμμάρψας δʼ ὅ γε χερσὶν ἑὴν ἐγκάτθετο νηδὺν
lines.translit: symmarpsas d' ho ge chersin heēn enkattheto nēdyn

i18n.en: But he seized her with his hands and put her into his belly,

lines.text: δείσας, μὴ τέξῃ κρατερώτερον ἄλλο κεραυνοῦ.
lines.translit: deisas mē texē kraterōteron allo keraunou

i18n.en: fearing that she might bear something stronger than the thunderbolt.

lines.text: τοὔνεκά μιν Κρονίδης ὑψίζυγος αἰθέρι ναίων
lines.translit: touneka min Kronidēs hypsizygos aitheri naiōn

i18n.en: Therefore the son of Kronos, throned on high, dwelling in the aether,

lines.text: κάππιεν ἐξαπίνης· ἣ δʼ αὐτίκα Παλλάδʼ Ἀθήνην
lines.translit: kappien exapinēs hē d' autika Pallad' Athēnēn

i18n.en: swallowed her suddenly; and she at once conceived Pallas Athena;

lines.text: κύσατο· τὴν μὲν ἔτικτε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε
lines.translit: kysato tēn men etikte patēr andrōn te theōn te

i18n.en: and the father of men and gods brought her forth

lines.text: πὰρ κορυφὴν Τρίτωνος ἐπʼ ὄχθῃσιν ποταμοῖο.
lines.translit: par koryphēn Tritōnos ep' ochthēsin potamoio

i18n.en: by the peak, beside the banks of the river Triton.

lines.text: Μῆτις δʼ αὖτε Ζηνὸς ὑπὸ σπλάγχνοις λελαθυῖα
lines.translit: Mētis d' aute Zēnos hypo splanchnois lelathyia

i18n.en: But Metis, hidden away beneath the vitals of Zeus,

notes.official: *Μῆτις … Ζηνὸς ὑπὸ σπλάγχνοις λελαθυῖα* 'Metis, hidden away beneath the vitals of Zeus' (929n): in the variant she remains within Zeus as *Ἀθηναίης μήτηρ* 'mother of Athena' and source of his counsel (929n–r) — the doublet's fuller statement of the swallowed-*mētis* motif of 886–900. `metis-metieta-cunning-counsel-network-theogony`; see on 886 and 929a.

lines.text: ἧστο, Ἀθηναίης μήτηρ, τέκταινα δικαίων
lines.translit: hēsto Athēnaiēs mētēr tektaina dikaiōn

i18n.en: remained, the mother of Athena, deviser of just things,

lines.text: πλεῖστα θεῶν τε ἰδυῖα καταθνητῶν τʼ ἀνθρώπων,
lines.translit: pleista theōn te idyia katathnētōn t' anthrōpōn

i18n.en: knowing most of gods and of mortal men.

lines.text: ἔνθα θεὰ παρέδεκτο ὅθεν παλάμαις περὶ πάντων
lines.translit: entha thea paredekto hothen palamais peri pantōn

i18n.en: There the goddess received that whereby, with her hands, above all

lines.text: ἀθανάτων ἐκέκασθʼ οἳ Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσιν,
lines.translit: athanatōn ekekasth' hoi Olympia dōmat' echousin

i18n.en: the immortals who have their homes on Olympos she excelled;

lines.text: αἰγίδα ποιήσασα φοβέστρατον ἔντος Ἀθήνης·
lines.translit: aigida poiēsasa phobestraton entos Athēnēs

i18n.en: for she made the aegis, Athena's army-routing armor.

notes.official: Within the variant supplement, line 929s (*αἰγίδα ποιήσασα φοβέστρατον ἔντος Ἀθήνης* 'she made the aegis, Athena's army-routing armour') is additionally athetized (*<del>*) in the edition — a secondary insertion even within the secondary block. Retained and translated unmarked per the athetized-lines convention, the double status (supplement + athetesis) recorded here. The *αἰγίς* is the storm-shield, left untranslated as a cultic object (cf. `aigiochos-aegis-bearer-zeus-epithet-theogony`, whose scope is extended to the Block-D aegis sites). Governed by `variant-passage-929a-929t-metis-doublet-theogony` and `athetized-lines-convention-theogony`.

lines.text: σὺν τῇ ἐγείνατό μιν πολεμήια τεύχεʼ ἔχουσαν.
lines.translit: syn tē egeinato min polemēia teuche' echousan

i18n.en: With it he brought her forth, wearing her war-gear.

lines.text: Ἐκ δʼ Ἀμφιτρίτης καὶ ἐρικτύπου Ἐννοσιγαίου
lines.translit: ek d' Amphitritēs kai eriktypou Ennosigaiou

i18n.en: And of Amphitrite and the loud-crashing Earth-Shaker

lines.text: Τρίτων εὐρυβίης γένετο μέγας, ὅστε θαλάσσης
lines.translit: Tritōn eurybiēs geneto megas hoste thalassēs

i18n.en: was born great, wide-ruling Triton, who,

lines.text: πυθμένʼ ἔχων παρὰ μητρὶ φίλῃ καὶ πατρὶ ἄνακτι
lines.translit: pythmen' echōn para mētri philē kai patri anakti

i18n.en: holding the depths of the sea beside his dear mother and his lordly father,

lines.text: ναίει χρύσεα δῶ, δεινὸς θεός. αὐτὰρ Ἄρηι
lines.translit: naiei chrysea dō deinos theos autar Arēi

i18n.en: dwells in golden halls, a dread god. And to Ares,

lines.text: ῥινοτόρῳ Κυθέρεια Φόβον καὶ Δεῖμον ἔτικτε
lines.translit: rhinotorō Kythereia Phobon kai Deimon etikte

i18n.en: the shield-piercer, Kythereia bore Phobos and Deimos,

notes.official: *Φόβον καὶ Δεῖμον* (934): transparent personifications — Phobos 'Rout/Panic', Deimos 'Terror/Fear' — and also cult-established war-daimones, sons of Ares. The surface transliterates 'Phobos and Deimos' as proper names (Reviewer revise, Block D review, sustained at sign-off), departing from Evelyn-White's translated 'Panic and Fear', for consistency with their sister *Ἁρμονίη* 'Harmonia', transliterated in the same clause (937), and with the cult-established *Ζῆλος/Νίκη/Κράτος/Βίη* transliterated at 384–385 (Block B) under `personified-abstractions-nyx-eris-brood-theogony`. The standing choice is the reference's translated pair; **the translate-vs-transliterate call is flagged for the Reviewer.**

lines.text: δεινούς, οἵτʼ ἀνδρῶν πυκινὰς κλονέουσι φάλαγγας
lines.translit: deinous hoit' andrōn pykinas kloneousi phalangas

i18n.en: dread gods, who throw into confusion the close ranks of men

lines.text: ἐν πολέμῳ κρυόεντι σὺν Ἄρηι πτολιπόρθῳ,
lines.translit: en polemō kryoenti syn Arēi ptoliporthō

i18n.en: in chill war, together with Ares, sacker of cities;

lines.text: Ἁρμονίην θʼ, ἣν Κάδμος ὑπέρθυμος θέτʼ ἄκοιτιν.
lines.translit: Harmoniēn th' hēn Kadmos hyperthymos thet' akoitin

i18n.en: and Harmonia, whom high-spirited Kadmos made his wife.

lines.text: Ζηνὶ δʼ ἄρʼ Ἀτλαντὶς Μαίη τέκε κύδιμον Ἑρμῆν,
lines.translit: Zēni d' ar' Atlantis Maiē teke kydimon Hermēn

i18n.en: And to Zeus, Maia, daughter of Atlas, bore glorious Hermes,

lines.text: κήρυκʼ ἀθανάτων, ἱερὸν λέχος εἰσαναβᾶσα.
lines.translit: kēryk' athanatōn hieron lechos eisanabasa

i18n.en: the herald of the immortals, having ascended his holy bed.

lines.text: Καδμείη δʼ ἄρα οἱ Σεμέλη τέκε φαίδιμον υἱὸν
lines.translit: Kadmeiē d' ara hoi Semelē teke phaidimon huion

i18n.en: And Semele, daughter of Kadmos, bore him a glorious son,

lines.text: μιχθεῖσʼ ἐν φιλότητι, Διώνυσον πολυγηθέα,
lines.translit: michtheis' en philotēti Diōnyson polygēthea

i18n.en: mingling in love—Dionysos, the giver of much joy,

lines.text: ἀθάνατον θνητή· νῦν δʼ ἀμφότεροι θεοί εἰσιν.
lines.translit: athanaton thnētē nyn d' amphoteroi theoi eisin

i18n.en: an immortal, though she was mortal; but now both are gods.

lines.text: Ἀλκμήνη δʼ ἄρʼ ἔτικτε βίην Ἡρακληείην
lines.translit: Alkmēnē d' ar' etikte biēn Hēraklēeiēn

i18n.en: And Alkmene bore the mighty Herakles,

lines.text: μιχθεῖσʼ ἐν φιλότητι Διὸς νεφεληγερέταο.
lines.translit: michtheis' en philotēti Dios nephelēgeretao

i18n.en: mingling in love with Zeus the cloud-gatherer.

lines.text: ἀγλαΐην δʼ Ἥφαιστος, ἀγακλυτὸς ἀμφιγυήεις,
lines.translit: aglaiēn d' Hēphaistos agaklytos amphigyēeis

i18n.en: And Aglaia—Hephaestus, the renowned Lame One,

lines.text: ὁπλοτάτην Χαρίτων θαλερὴν ποιήσατʼ ἄκοιτιν.
lines.translit: hoplotatēn Charitōn thalerēn poiēsat' akoitin
